title: Phased-Array Stirring, No Turntable
new_elements: Beam-steered RF feed (Electronically moves hot spots, replacing the glass turntable.); Even heating of any dish shape (Rectangular dishes fit and nothing jams.)
rationale: There is no plate to seat correctly and no rotation rules to learn.
judge_comment: Beam steering removes the turntable and its rules, but it is a narrower usability gain and it depends on the same solid-state RF hardware.

title: Food Temperature Probe Stick
new_elements: Tethered microwave-safe probe (Stick it in the food and the oven stops at the target core temperature.); Core temperature control (Replaces the timer.)
rationale: Stick it in and walk away; it can't be gotten wrong.
judge_comment: A tethered probe gives a clear goal-based interaction, but it adds a step and an accessory, and probes in microwaves are tricky.

title: Metal Detection Guard
new_elements: Reflected-power arc detector (Detects metal or foil and stops instantly.); Mistake-proof operation (No need to learn which containers are safe.); Users must know microwave-safe rules (Hidden knowledge required for safe use.)
rationale: The machine protects users from the knowledge gap.
judge_comment: Arc or reflected-power detection is a real safety feature, but it addresses safety more than operating simplicity and is only loosely a substitution.

title: Talking Progress Instead of Bell
new_elements: Voice prompt speaker (Says 'Your soup is ready, stir and enjoy'.); Spoken guidance and completion (Replaces the clockwork bell.)
rationale: The appliance explains itself in plain words.
judge_comment: Voice prompts are easy to build and mildly helpful, but they are common and replace only the bell.

title: Doneness Sticker Labels
new_elements: Thermochromic food-pack stickers (A sticker on the container turns green when hot enough.); Package-level done cue (Supplements or replaces the timer bell.)
rationale: A green signal means ready to everyone.
judge_comment: Thermochromic stickers give an intuitive done signal, but they depend on food makers and are poor at signaling uneven heating.

title: Keep-Warm Auto Hold
new_elements: Low-duty hold controller (Keeps food warm until the door opens.); Forgiving completion (Replaces the need to respond to the bell promptly.)
rationale: There is no penalty for forgetting the food, so users have no rules to learn.
judge_comment: Keep-warm hold is practical and forgiving, but it only mitigates the bell and does not simplify starting or setting the oven, and it is not a radical substitution.

title: Halogen Lamp Grill
new_elements: Quartz halogen light-and-browning lamp (The interior lamp is upsized to an IR halogen that both lights and browns.)
rationale: One part, two jobs, with no extra controls.
judge_comment: A halogen browning lamp is plausible and merges two functions, but it does little for no-learning-curve operation and the browning is not automatic.

title: Push-Anywhere Door
new_elements: Push-to-open magnetic latch (Press anywhere on the door to pop it open; no button needs to be found.)
rationale: The door opens with any intuitive push.
judge_comment: A push-anywhere door is intuitive and feasible, but it simplifies only opening, not the main operation.

title: Single Knob, Auto Power
new_elements: Infers power level from chosen time (Long times auto-reduce power to avoid scorching; short times use full power.)
rationale: Two knobs become one.
judge_comment: Practical simplification that merges two controls into one, but it is incremental, and silently overriding power can surprise users.

title: Bell-Jar Microwave
new_elements: Lowering RF dome over plate (The user sets the plate on a base and pulls down a meshed dome, which seals and starts heating.)
rationale: Covering a plate is an instinctive gesture.
judge_comment: The gesture of covering a plate is intuitive and distinctive, but a meshed dome that seals RF safely and starts heating is hard to build, and it does not say how heating time gets set.

title: Talk-to-Heat
new_elements: Offline voice command module (Understands phrases like 'warm my coffee'.)
rationale: Speech requires no interface learning.
judge_comment: Voice control needs no learning in principle, but it is a common idea, and offline recognition can be unreliable and awkward in noisy kitchens.

title: Dummy-Load Floor Tile
new_elements: Lossy ceramic absorber tile (Absorbs RF safely if the oven is run empty, preventing magnetron overheating.)
rationale: Running it empty is harmless, so there is no 'never run empty' rule.
judge_comment: A lossy ceramic load removes the run-empty risk and is plausible, but it only addresses one minor rule and does little for the learning curve.

title: Fan-Driven Mode Stirrer
new_elements: Air-driven metal mode stirrer (The cooling airflow spins a reflector paddle that scatters RF evenly.)
rationale: No turntable, so oversized dishes never jam.
judge_comment: Air-driven mode stirrers are plausible, and some microwaves already use stirrers, but the connection to ease of operation is indirect.

title: Voice Countdown
new_elements: Spoken status chip (Says 'ten seconds left' and 'ready, careful, hot', replacing the bell.)
rationale: Plain-language feedback explains itself.
judge_comment: Spoken status is easy and helpful for feedback, but it replaces only the bell and does not simplify the operating controls, so it is an incremental step.

title: Drawer Microwave
new_elements: Sliding drawer cavity on rails (The cavity slides out like a kitchen drawer, removing the need for hinges or a latch button.)
rationale: Pulling a drawer open is a universal gesture with no button to find.
judge_comment: Drawer microwaves exist, so novelty is moderate; the gesture is familiar but it doesn't address setting time or power.

title: Thermal Pop-Disc Finish
new_elements: Bimetal snap-disc thermostat probe (A ceramic-shielded probe in the food snaps open at 70°C and cuts the magnetron.)
rationale: Food is heated until it is hot, so no time decision is needed.
judge_comment: A snap-disc probe that stops at a set temperature is a neat mechanical idea, but a probe inside food in a microwave raises arcing and usability problems, and one fixed temperature suits few foods.

title: Packaging Barcode Cook
new_elements: Door-mounted barcode scanner (Scans the ready-meal barcode and loads the manufacturer's heating profile.)
rationale: Users no longer need to read small instructions on the box.
judge_comment: A barcode scan removes reading the box, but it depends on a manufacturer profile database and only covers packaged meals, so it adds a step for everything else.

title: Say What You Want
new_elements: Offline voice command module (A low-cost keyword chip understands phrases like 'warm coffee' or 'defrost bread'.)
rationale: Natural speech replaces dials altogether.
judge_comment: Offline keyword voice control is intuitive and feasible with cheap chips, but it is a fairly obvious idea and can fail in noisy kitchens.

title: Three Big Preset Buttons
new_elements: Three oversized preset buttons (Mug, Plate and Popcorn buttons, each with a fixed time and power.)
rationale: Three obvious choices cover most real-world use.
judge_comment: Three big presets are very simple and cheap but are a conventional, incremental idea rather than a radical one.

title: Roll-Top Tambour Door
new_elements: Metal-slat roll-top door (Interlocking choke-groove slats roll up into the roof like a bread bin.)
rationale: The door slides up out of the way and never swings into the user.
judge_comment: A roll-top door is intuitive and avoids swing clearance, but microwave choke sealing and cleaning of the slats are difficult.

title: Gentle-Strong Inverter Knob
new_elements: Inverter power supply with continuous knob (A stepless 'gentle to strong' control delivers true variable power instead of duty cycling.)
rationale: Food heats evenly with no cold spots to troubleshoot, and the knob behaves like a volume control.
judge_comment: Inverter microwaves already exist, and a single stepless knob is intuitive, but the user still has to choose a power setting.

title: Mass-Driven Power
new_elements: Auto-selects power from food mass (Small loads get lower power to avoid explosions or overheating.)
rationale: The power level is chosen automatically, so the user never has to think about it.
judge_comment: Automatic power selection removes a decision, but weighing food in a microwave is hard and the mechanism is vague.

title: RFID Smart Plate
new_elements: Microwave-safe RFID plate (A shielded tag in the plate remembers each user's preferred reheat settings.)
rationale: Each person's own plate heats the way they like it with no setup.
judge_comment: A plate that remembers each person's settings is an interesting idea, but it needs setup and a shielded tag in the plate is difficult to build.

title: Touch-Anywhere Soft Open
new_elements: Push-to-open door with gas spring (Pressing anywhere on the door releases a touch latch and a gas strut swings it open gently.)
rationale: There is no specific button to locate, which suits users with arthritic hands.
judge_comment: Push-anywhere door opening removes the need to find a button and is plausible, but it only simplifies one small step and is not very radical.

title: Invisible-Mesh Glass Door
new_elements: ITO-coated transparent door (A transparent conductive oxide film shields the RF and gives a clear view.); Transparent conductive oxide shielding (Indium tin oxide or a silver nanowire layer reflects 2.45 GHz while passing visible light.)
rationale: The user can simply look at the food as with a pot on a stove, with no mesh blur and no lamp needed.
judge_comment: A transparent conductive door would give a clearer view, but ITO or nanowire films struggle to shield 2.45 GHz at high power, and the link to ease of use is only indirect.

title: Pull-Handle Door
new_elements: Grab-and-pull handle latch (Pulling an integrated handle releases the latch, so there is no separate button to find.)
rationale: The oven opens like every cupboard and fridge door.
judge_comment: Pull handles are already common and only address door opening, a small part of operation.

title: Magnetic Fridge-Style Door
new_elements: Magnetic door closure with reed interlock (A magnet holds the door closed, and redundant reed and Hall sensors replace the microswitches.)
rationale: The door needs only a push to close and a tug to open.
judge_comment: A magnetic door closure is intuitive, but safety interlock requirements for microwave leakage make it harder to certify.

title: NFC Lid Tags
new_elements: NFC reader under tray (Reads a tag printed on food lids and storage boxes to set the program.)
rationale: Putting the container in the oven is all the operation required.
judge_comment: Zero-step operation is appealing, but it needs tagged containers and ecosystem adoption, and NFC near a microwave cavity is difficult.

title: Talking Done Chime
new_elements: Voice playback chip (Speaks a message such as 'Your soup is ready, careful, it's hot.')
rationale: Plain words remove any ambiguity about the oven's state.
judge_comment: A voice chip is easy to build and clearer than a beep, but it only helps with the completion signal, not with operating the oven.

title: Single Sensor Interlock Module
new_elements: Sealed Hall-effect interlock module (One self-monitoring module with dual Hall sensors replaces three microswitches.)
rationale: There is no fiddly door alignment, and the oven always starts when the door is shut.
judge_comment: Concrete and plausible substitution of three microswitches, but it is mostly invisible to the user and only marginally helps operation simplicity.

title: Wave-to-Add
new_elements: IR proximity gesture sensor (Each hand wave adds 30 s, and holding the hand still stops cooking.)
rationale: It works without touch, even with messy hands, and needs no buttons.
judge_comment: Touchless wave-to-add is intuitive for the simple case, but accidental triggers, hand-still stopping and the lack of feedback make it less reliable.

title: Heat-Map Door
new_elements: Thermal camera door display (A low-resolution thermal sensor shows a colour heat map of the food on the door.)
rationale: The user sees which parts are still cold, so they don't have to guess.
judge_comment: A thermal view helps users judge doneness, but it adds a display and doesn't remove the need to operate controls; it also isn't a substitution of cheaper parts.

title: Mains-Counting Electronic Timer
new_elements: Mains-cycle counter timer (A cheap IC counts 50/60 Hz cycles behind the same familiar knob.)
rationale: It keeps the familiar knob and makes short times precise.
judge_comment: This is a cheap and very feasible substitution that keeps the familiar knob, but it is incremental and barely reduces learning.

title: Defrost Bag Pocket
new_elements: Freezer-icon contact pad (A frost-sensing thermistor in the floor detects frozen food and runs the defrost program automatically.)
rationale: The oven recognizes frozen food itself, so the user never has to choose 'defrost'.
judge_comment: Automatic detection of frozen food removes a decision, but a floor thermistor sensing frozen food through a container is unreliable.

title: Sand-Glass Visual Timer
new_elements: Illuminated draining bar (A vertical light column on the door drains like an hourglass as time runs.); Glanceable remaining time (Replaces the small numbers on the clockwork knob.); Tiny knob markings are hard to read (Remaining time is shown only by fine print on the dial.)
rationale: An hourglass metaphor is understood across ages and cultures.
judge_comment: An easy-to-build, universally understood remaining-time display that improves readability, but it only marginally reduces the learning curve and is not radical.

title: Single Full-Power Magnetron
new_elements: Fixed-power supply (Removes the duty-cycle cam entirely; the only control is time.); One-variable control (Halves the number of decisions the user must make.); Power cam adds cost and confusion (The power knob is rarely moved but often misunderstood.)
rationale: With just one control, there is nothing to get wrong.
judge_comment: A single time-only control is simple and easy to build, but it removes functionality and is not very radical.

title: Mode Stirrer Replaces Turntable
new_elements: Rotating metal mode stirrer (A hidden fan-blade reflector in the ceiling distributes the microwaves.); Even heating with a flat floor (No glass plate to seat, drop or misalign.); Turntable must be correctly seated (A misplaced plate or roller ring jams or rattles.)
rationale: There are no loose parts to assemble, so users simply put food in.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are already common in microwaves, and removing the turntable only slightly reduces the user's setup burden.

title: Magnetic Door, No Button
new_elements: Magnetic catch with pull handle (Replaces the push-release button with a simple pull-to-open door like a fridge.); Open by pulling (Uses a universally familiar door action.); Hidden push-release button (First-time users search for how to open the door.)
rationale: Everyone knows how to open a fridge door.
judge_comment: Easy and familiar door opening, but it is a minor usability tweak and not radical, and it doesn't address operating the controls.

title: Drawer Microwave
new_elements: Slide-out cavity drawer (Replaces the hinged door and push button; the drawer self-closes softly.); Top-down loading (Food is placed from above with no reaching into a box.); Awkward reach into cavity (Hot dishes must be pulled out at an awkward angle.)
rationale: Opening a drawer is intuitive and also safer.
judge_comment: A drawer is intuitive to open, but it doesn't simplify programming, and the awkward retrieval of hot dishes works against ease of use.

title: Passive Wireless Probe Plate
new_elements: SAW-sensor probe spike (A battery-free probe built into the plate or lid reports the core temperature.); Core-temperature stop (Prevents a cold centre in reheated food.); Cold centres (Food is hot outside but cold inside after a fixed time.)
rationale: It removes the stir-and-retry routine users otherwise have to learn.
judge_comment: A battery-free probe in the plate gives automatic doneness, but SAW sensors survive microwaves poorly and the probe adds a handling step.

title: Controlless Microwave
new_elements: Sensor fusion controller (Weight, IR and humidity sensors together decide everything.); Close door, get hot food (No knobs, buttons or display at all.); Any control is a learning step (Every control surface is something the user must learn.)
rationale: Zero controls means zero learning curve.
judge_comment: Zero controls would remove the learning curve entirely, but sensing food type and doneness reliably is very hard and users lose control.

title: Traffic-Light Door Frame
new_elements: RGB door-frame strip (Red = heating, amber = resting, green = ready to eat.); Colour-coded state (Replaces the bell and lamp as status indicators.); No resting-time guidance (Users take food out too early and it is unevenly hot.)
rationale: Traffic-light colours are universally understood.
judge_comment: Simple, feasible status indicator, but it only communicates state and does not simplify setting input; the resting-time idea is somewhat helpful.

title: Hot-Spot Aware Power
new_elements: IR array thermal map (Automatically reduces power when hot spots appear.); Automatic power modulation (Replaces the user-chosen power step.); Exploding or splattering food (High power on dense food causes eruptions.)
rationale: Users never need to learn when to lower the power.
judge_comment: IR thermal mapping with automatic power modulation removes the need to choose a power level, but it only covers one setting and the SUBSTITUTE link is loose.

title: Steam-Sniffer Stop
new_elements: Exhaust humidity sensor (Detects the steam burst that signals food is heated through and ends the cycle.)
rationale: The microwave decides when the food is done, so the user does not have to.
judge_comment: Humidity-sensor auto-stop is plausible and simple for the user, but sensor cooking already exists in the market.

title: Power-by-Container Lids
new_elements: Shielded-pattern cookware lids (Lids with different printed metal-mesh coverage pass a set fraction of the field: a defrost lid, a reheat lid, or no lid.)
rationale: The power level is chosen by grabbing the lid with the matching colour; there is no knob to understand.
judge_comment: Very novel, passive power selection by lid, but requires buying special lids and partial-shielding physics is tricky; it also adds a new thing to learn.

title: Gravity Top-Lid
new_elements: Top-loading gravity-closing lid (A chest-style lid falls shut under its own weight and has no latch.)
rationale: Like a rice cooker lid, it is obvious and impossible to leave half-latched.
judge_comment: A gravity-closing top lid is obvious to use and prevents half-latching, but the lid must still seal against leakage and reaching into a top-loading cavity is awkward.

title: Roll-Top Tambour Door
new_elements: Shielded roll-top tambour door (Conductive slats roll up into the cabinet like a bread bin.)
rationale: The door never swings into the user and slides with one finger.
judge_comment: A roll-top tambour door is novel and avoids swing clearance, but conductive slats leak at the joints and are hard to clean.

title: Spin-the-Plate Timer
new_elements: Turntable-wound spring timer (Turning the glass plate by hand winds the timer; the plate then unwinds while cooking.)
rationale: The control sits where the food is, so the setting action is part of loading the food.
judge_comment: Winding the timer by turning the plate is wild and clever, but the turntable would need a mechanical link and sits awkwardly with the sealed cavity and the plate's role in cooking.

title: Revolving Carousel Door
new_elements: Rotating drum compartment (A bank-teller-style drum rotates food inside, so the cavity is never open to the user.)
rationale: Rotating the drum both loads the food and starts heating, with no latching or opening steps.
judge_comment: A rotating drum is very radical and removes the door steps, but RF sealing, cleaning and cost make it hard to realize.

title: Self-Shielding Lunchbox
new_elements: Metal-walled smart container with RF window port (The container is its own Faraday cage and docks onto an emitter base.)
rationale: Dropping the box on the dock is the entire operation.
judge_comment: Drop-on-dock operation is the simplest possible, but it requires a proprietary container and RF coupling through a window, which is dubious.

title: Write-On Dial Ring
new_elements: Erasable marker ring around timer knob (Family members mark positions such as 'Grandma's soup'.)
rationale: Personal labels replace generic numbers at almost zero cost.
judge_comment: A very cheap, practical personalization aid that helps recall, but it is a minor tweak rather than a radical substitution.

title: Again Button
new_elements: Memory cam 'same again' button (A mechanical memory re-sets the timer to the last used position.)
rationale: Routine users repeat their daily coffee warm-up with one press.
judge_comment: A mechanical same-again button is useful for routine tasks, but it is an incremental, familiar idea.

title: Foot-Pedal Door
new_elements: Cable-linked counter-edge foot pedal (Pressing the pedal releases the latch for hands-full opening.)
rationale: Pedal-bin familiarity means instant use with hot plates in hand.
judge_comment: A familiar pedal helps with hands-full opening, but it only affects opening and does not simplify operation overall.

title: Elbow Paddle Door Edge
new_elements: Full-height paddle release along door edge (The entire door edge is the release; there is no small button to locate.)
rationale: A huge target suits arthritic hands and needs no fine motor skill.
judge_comment: A large door-edge release is simple and accessible, but it only improves the door opening and is not very radical.

title: Cup-Holder Coffee Port
new_elements: Choke-sealed mug socket (Sliding a mug into the side socket heats it to drinking temperature; there is no door to open.)
rationale: The most common elderly use, reheating a drink, becomes a single insertion.
judge_comment: A door-less mug socket is a striking idea that makes drink reheating trivial, but it covers only one use case and raises safety and leakage concerns.

title: Popcorn Ear
new_elements: Acoustic pop counter microphone (A microphone detects the falling rate of popping and stops cooking.)
rationale: No burnt popcorn and no guessing: the oven listens and decides.
judge_comment: Acoustic popcorn detection exists in some ovens and only serves one food, so it is a narrow help for simplicity.

title: Quartz Clock Movement Timer
new_elements: Mass-produced quartz movement timer (A wall-clock quartz module drives the cam, giving precision independent of mains frequency.)
rationale: Short times become accurate, so results match user expectations without fiddling.
judge_comment: A quartz movement improves accuracy but does little for ease of operation, and it's an obvious, incremental swap.

title: Defrost Dome Accessory
new_elements: Partially shielding defrost dome (A perforated metal-patterned cover reduces absorbed power for delicate food.)
rationale: Covering the food to cook it gently is a physical, obvious gesture.
judge_comment: Plausible, simple accessory, but metal near microwaves risks arcing and it only adds a single gentle mode.

title: Talk-to-Cook
new_elements: Offline keyword speech chip (Recognises commands such as 'heat one minute', 'soup' and 'stop'.)
rationale: Speaking naturally is the lowest learning curve, especially for users with poor sight.
judge_comment: Voice control is easy to use and technically mature, but it is not very radical and noisy kitchens can cause errors.

title: Camera Food Recognition
new_elements: Cavity camera with food classifier (Identifies the food type and quantity and auto-selects time and power.)
rationale: The machine works out what you are heating, so the only action is pressing go.
judge_comment: Auto recognition minimizes user action, but accuracy, cost and steam on the lens are challenges, and it adds rather than substitutes parts.

title: Garage-Door Flip-Up
new_elements: Top-hinged gas-strut door (The door lifts up, stays open on a strut, and closes by gravity onto the interlock.)
rationale: It needs one push up and one push down, with no latch to discover.
judge_comment: A gas-strut flip-up door is feasible and intuitive, but it is an incremental change that only simplifies the door.

title: Electromagnet-Only Lock
new_elements: Cooking-only electromagnetic door hold (The door swings freely when idle and is held only while the magnetron runs.)
rationale: No button exists; the door simply opens whenever it is safe.
judge_comment: Removing the door button is a clever simplification, but a door that swings free when idle has safety and interlock questions, and it only partly helps operation.

title: Foot-Tap Kick Panel
new_elements: Base kick switch (A tap on the lower front panel opens the door; a second tap starts a 1-minute cycle.)
rationale: It allows hands-full operation with a single universal gesture.
judge_comment: A kick switch is simple and feasible and helps with hands-full use, but a fixed 1-minute cycle is limiting and accidental kicks are a risk.

title: Region-Free Mechanical Core
new_elements: Mains-independent flywheel-governed timer (A centrifugal governor sets the timer speed regardless of 50/60 Hz.)
rationale: The same dial markings are correct worldwide, so travellers and migrants need no relearning.
judge_comment: A centrifugal governor timer is a distinctive mechanical substitution, but it only addresses the 50/60 Hz issue, which isn't the main learning-curve barrier.

title: Door-Close Autostart
new_elements: Starts the default heat cycle when the door closes (The interlock circuit doubles as the start trigger and runs a 1-minute preset unless the user changes it.)
rationale: Closing the door is the only action needed, so there is no start step to learn.
judge_comment: Removes the start step and is easy to build, but unintended starts (for example when the cavity is empty) are a safety concern and it is not very radical.

title: Glowing Done Ring
new_elements: Colour-changing LED halo (A ring around the door glows amber while heating and green when the food is ready.)
rationale: Traffic-light colours are understood by everyone, including kids and guests.
judge_comment: An easy-to-understand status indicator that helps readability, but it doesn't substitute the core operation or controls and is fairly obvious.

title: Shrinking Light Bar Timer
new_elements: LED countdown bar (Segments switch off one by one as time elapses and can be read from across the room.)
rationale: A shrinking bar shows 'how much is left' with no numbers to interpret.
judge_comment: A visual countdown bar substitutes numerals intuitively but doesn't simplify input and is a common idea.

title: Instructions on the Door
new_elements: Embossed quick-guide fascia (Three picture steps moulded into the fascia (food in, dial, wait for the ding) replace the manual.)
rationale: The guidance is permanently where the user's eyes already are.
judge_comment: Embossed pictorial instructions directly cut the learning curve and are cheap, but they are far from radical and many microwaves already print similar guides.

title: Drop-Down Shelf Door
new_elements: Bottom-hinged flap door (The door folds down like an oven door, acts as a resting shelf and closes by lifting.)
rationale: It works the same whether the user is left- or right-handed and is familiar from ovens, with no clearance confusion.
judge_comment: A drop-down door is familiar and handedness-neutral, but spill risk and the mechanical changes give only a modest operational gain.

title: Large Tactile Shape Knob
new_elements: Oversized detented knob with shape cues (A palm-sized knob with strong clicks every 30 s and raised icons that can be read by touch.)
rationale: Clicks and shapes give feedback that works for anyone, including elderly users.
judge_comment: Easy to use and accessible, but large detented knobs are common and barely radical.

title: Dish-Shape Recognition Tray
new_elements: Capacitive footprint-sensing tray (Senses whether a mug, bowl or plate is present from its contact pattern and chooses the profile.)
rationale: The container shape implies the task, so no input is needed.
judge_comment: Removes input entirely, but capacitive sensing can't reliably tell the dish or food, so the inferred profile is often wrong.

title: Hold-Gaze Proximity Start
new_elements: Wave-to-add-time proximity sensor (Each wave of a hand in front of the door adds 30 s, so the oven can be used with greasy hands.)
rationale: A natural gesture with no buttons to locate or decode.
judge_comment: Wave-to-add-time is intuitive and hands-free, but it is ambiguous with no feedback, and wave counts could be accidental.

title: Weigh-and-Heat Turntable
new_elements: Load-cell turntable (A strain gauge under the tray weighs the food and calculates the heating time.); Strain-gauge weighing (Cheap kitchen-scale sensor.)
rationale: The machine works out the time from the food's weight, so the user never has to guess.
judge_comment: Weight alone doesn't determine heating time (food type, starting temperature), and a load cell under a rotating turntable is awkward, though it removes time guessing.

title: Passive Defrost Tray
new_elements: Lossy ceramic defrost tray (A tray with water-filled channels absorbs part of the RF, giving gentle heat without a power setting.)
rationale: Defrosting becomes 'use the defrost plate' rather than understanding power levels.
judge_comment: Passive lossy tray removes power-level knowledge for defrosting, though water-channel absorption control is uncertain and only covers one function.

title: Pull-Handle Door
new_elements: Magnetic-catch pull handle (A fridge-style magnetic latch replaces the push button and latch lever.)
rationale: Everyone already knows how to pull a fridge door open, so there is no button to find.
judge_comment: Familiar pull handle is easy and feasible, but only addresses door opening and is a modest change.

title: Field-Powered Glow Cavity
new_elements: Wireless neon glow tube (A sealed gas tube lit directly by the microwave field glows only while heating, with no wiring.)
rationale: A glow means 'heating' and darkness means 'done', which is self-explanatory feedback.
judge_comment: A glow-as-status cue is wildly novel and intuitive, but gas tubes in a cavity risk arcing and uneven lighting, and it is unreliable as a signal.

title: Mode Stirrer Instead of Turntable
new_elements: Ceiling mode-stirrer fan (A rotating metal paddle scatters the field, so the cavity floor is flat with no tray.)
rationale: There is no tray to seat correctly or knock off its rollers; just put the food anywhere.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are already used in many microwaves, and removing the tray helps only marginally with operation.

title: Steam Whistle Done Signal
new_elements: Steam-driven vent whistle (Food steam escaping through the vent blows a kettle-style whistle when food is hot.)
rationale: The kettle whistle is a universally known 'it's hot' cue.
judge_comment: An intuitive, familiar done cue, but it only signals that food is hot and not that cooking is complete, and it is unreliable for dry foods and covered dishes.

title: Magnetic Reed Interlock
new_elements: Sealed reed-switch interlock trio (Door magnets actuate sealed reeds with no hooks to misalign.)
rationale: The door works with a soft close, with no slamming or jiggling needed to start.
judge_comment: A reed-switch interlock removes door-latch fussiness, but safety-interlock redundancy requirements make the swap harder and the user benefit is modest.

title: Popcorn Ear
new_elements: Acoustic pop-interval microphone (Stops when the gaps between pops exceed 2 s.)
rationale: No more guessing popcorn times or burning the bag.
judge_comment: Acoustic popcorn detection already exists in some microwaves, so it is only useful for one task, though it is concrete and works.

title: READY Flag
new_elements: Spring flip-up READY flag (The timer cam releases a bright mechanical flag on top of the cabinet.)
rationale: The flag stays visible from across the room even after a missed ding.
judge_comment: A mechanical flag is a charming substitution for a beep, but it aids end-of-cycle awareness rather than operating the microwave, so it only weakly serves the no-learning-curve need.

title: Same-As-Last-Time Button
new_elements: Repeats previous cycle (Memory recalls the last time and power used.)
rationale: Routines like morning coffee become a single press.
judge_comment: A repeat button is simple and useful for routines, but many microwaves already have similar functions and it does nothing for first use.

title: Integrated Floor Platter
new_elements: Sealed rotating floor disc (A flush ceramic disc built into the floor that cannot be removed or misplaced.)
rationale: There is no reassembly after washing, so the oven is always ready to use correctly.
judge_comment: A fixed floor disc removes the removable-plate setup error, but it makes cleaning harder and mainly addresses maintenance, not operation.

title: Nucleation Mug Zone
new_elements: Etched nucleation spot on the floor (An etched spot marks where liquids go, paired with a supplied nucleation-etched mug that releases bubbles so water cannot superheat.)
rationale: Users get safe drinks without having to know about the superheating risk.
judge_comment: The etched spot and nucleation mug are clever for safety, but they depend on a supplied mug and have little effect on operational simplicity.

title: Sand-Glass Visual Countdown
new_elements: Shrinking light-bar countdown (A glowing bar drains like an hourglass to show the remaining time.)
rationale: Remaining time is understood without reading numbers.
judge_comment: Easy to implement and intuitive for reading time, but it only aids display, not operation, and is hardly radical.

title: Food-Shelf Defrost Height
new_elements: Low-field rack slot (Placing food on a marked upper rack in a weak-field zone automatically gives gentle heat.)
rationale: Where you put the food decides the power, which is an intuitive spatial rule.
judge_comment: Spatial power selection is intuitive, but creating reliable weak-field zones in a cavity is technically doubtful.

title: Steam-Sniffer Auto Stop
new_elements: Exhaust humidity sensor (Detects the steam burst released when food is hot.); Stops heating when food steams (Ends the cycle based on food state instead of a clock.)
rationale: The user no longer needs to guess cooking times because the oven stops when the food is done.
judge_comment: Humidity-sensing auto stop already exists in sensor-cook models, so it is only moderately new, but it does serve the need well.

title: Phased-Array Beam Steering, No Turntable
new_elements: Multi-port phased RF antennas (Electronically steer energy toward cold spots.)
rationale: There is no turntable to seat, remove or clean, and food heats evenly without user effort.
judge_comment: Electronic beam steering is a bold way to remove the turntable, but it is complex and expensive, and its link to operating simplicity is weak.

title: Talking Done Voice
new_elements: Voice chip speaker (Says 'Done, let it stand one minute' instead of ringing a bell.)
rationale: The oven tells the user what to do next in plain words.
judge_comment: Spoken guidance is helpful and cheap to build, but it only affects the end of the cycle and does not simplify starting it.

title: Hall-Effect Safety Interlock
new_elements: Dual Hall sensors + safety IC (Contactless sensing that cannot weld shut, replacing three microswitches.)
rationale: A lighter, gentler door with no stiff click to force makes operation effortless.
judge_comment: Hall sensors are plausible and concrete, but the benefit to a no-learning-curve experience is indirect.

title: Nucleation-Etched Turntable
new_elements: Micro-etched glass plate centre (Textured spots help steam bubbles form at the base of cups.)
rationale: It reduces superheating risk without the user knowing to add a spoon or stir.
judge_comment: Etched nucleation sites are a clever passive safety fix, but their effectiveness is uncertain and they only partly address ease of operation.

title: Self-Resetting PTC Protection
new_elements: PTC thermistor on magnetron (Limits current smoothly and resets itself, replacing the snap disc.)
rationale: There is no mysterious dead oven after overheating, because it just recovers.
judge_comment: A self-resetting protector avoids a confusing dead-oven state, which is a real if minor usability gain, though PTC suitability for magnetron current is doubtful.

title: Ferrite-Rubber Door Gasket
new_elements: Microwave-absorbing ferrite elastomer seal (Replaces the precision-stamped choke rim.)
rationale: A forgiving seal tolerates sloppy door closing.
judge_comment: Ferrite elastomer seals exist and are plausible, but the benefit to user simplicity is indirect.

title: One Knob To Rule Them All
new_elements: Single combined time-power knob (One dial has a gentle arc (low power) and a hot arc (full power), each graduated in minutes.)
rationale: Halving the controls to a single dial removes the need to work out which knob does what.
judge_comment: Simple and cheap, but a dual-arc dial still requires some understanding and is an incremental change.

title: Thermochromic Done-Indicator Plate
new_elements: Thermochromic-glazed turntable (The plate rim turns from blue to red when the food above is hot.)
rationale: Colour-change doneness can be read at a glance through the window, with nothing to interpret.
judge_comment: An at-a-glance doneness signal is intuitive, but a thermochromic glaze on a turntable reflects plate temperature rather than food temperature, and it doesn't simplify the controls.

title: Elbow Paddle Opener
new_elements: Large bottom paddle release (A full-width bar can be pressed with an elbow or wrist while holding a plate.)
rationale: It removes the awkward two-hand dance with arthritic fingers.
judge_comment: A bottom paddle release is easy and plausible and helps accessibility, but it is incremental and does not touch control complexity.

title: Top-Loading Lift Lid
new_elements: Gravity-closing top lid (The cavity is loaded from above like a chest; lid weight closes and seals it.)
rationale: Lifting a lid like a pot lid is obvious, and gravity does the latching.
judge_comment: A top-loading lid is intuitive, but it needs a safe interlock, microwave sealing and a lid that works reliably, and reaching into a chest is awkward.

title: Stamped Flexure Hinge
new_elements: Single-piece spring-steel flexure hinge (Replaces the pin hinges and adds soft-close spring return.)
rationale: The door closes itself gently and fully, so users cannot leave it 'almost shut' and wonder why it won't start.
judge_comment: A practical flexure hinge that closes the door, but it is only an incremental fix with a modest effect on ease of operation.

title: Voice Command Only
new_elements: Offline keyword voice module (Understands 'warm my tea', 'two minutes', 'stop' without a network.)
rationale: Speaking normally is the most natural interface and replaces every knob.
judge_comment: Offline voice control removes the need to learn a panel, but voice appliances are already common and the idea is not very radical.

title: Mains-Agnostic Universal Unit
new_elements: Universal-input switch-mode supply with crystal timing (One SKU works on 100-240 V at 50/60 Hz; the timer is no longer tied to mains frequency.)
rationale: Identical behaviour everywhere means instructions and habits never change, even when the user travels or moves.
judge_comment: A universal power supply with crystal timing is concrete and feasible, but it barely affects day-to-day ease of use.

title: Door-Close-to-Start
new_elements: Clockwork timer knob (Existing timer knob, which also acts as the start switch); Door-actuated start switch (Closing the door starts sensor cooking; opening it stops); Start by closing door (Starting needs no separate action)
rationale: Starting the oven becomes a natural part of loading it.
judge_comment: Starting by closing the door removes a step and is easy to build. It risks accidental starts, and the knob is still needed, so it is only a partial simplification.

title: Natural Voice Command
new_elements: Clockwork timer knob (Existing timer knob from base_product meta); Offline voice module (Understands phrases like "warm my coffee" or "defrost chicken"); Operate by plain speech (No interface to learn)
rationale: Talking needs no training.
judge_comment: Voice control needs no learning in principle, but it is a common idea and is less reliable in noisy kitchens, with accents and for users who are unsure what to say.

title: Drawer Microwave
new_elements: Door push-release button (Existing hinged door and release from base_product meta); Pull-out drawer cavity (Food is placed in from above, like a drawer); Top-down loading (Easier to reach and see into)
rationale: Everyone knows how a drawer works.
judge_comment: A drawer is a familiar metaphor and a notable departure, but the drawer microwave already exists and the idea does not simplify the controls.

title: LED Strip Lamp
new_elements: Incandescent interior lamp (Existing 20-25 W bulb from base_product meta); Shielded LED strip (Uses about 1 W and lasts the product's lifetime); Illuminate cavity without maintenance (No bulb ever needs replacing)
rationale: Removing bulb replacement removes a hidden maintenance task the user would otherwise have to learn.
judge_comment: A valid and feasible substitution, but an LED lamp does little for learning-free operation and is not radical.

title: Mesh-Coated Glass Dome Casing
new_elements: Incandescent interior lamp (Existing lamp from base_product meta); Transparent ITO-shielded glass cavity (A conductive transparent coating blocks microwaves while ambient light shows the food); See food from any angle (No lamp and no perforated door needed)
rationale: Seeing the food at all times makes the oven self-explanatory.
judge_comment: A transparent conductive glass cavity is a wild idea, but ITO shielding at microwave leakage levels, durability and heat are doubtful.

title: Flat-Floor Mode Stirrer
new_elements: Glass turntable (Existing turntable and drive from base_product meta); Hidden mode stirrer fan (A rotating metal vane in the ceiling evens out the field); Even heating without moving parts in cavity (Flat floor that wipes clean)
rationale: There is no tray to seat, lose or break, and any dish size fits.
judge_comment: A mode stirrer in place of the turntable is plausible and used in real ovens, but it only loosely relates to ease of operation.

title: Top-Loading Lift-Lid Pod
new_elements: Door push-release button (Existing front door from base_product meta); Hinged dome lid (Lift and close like a rice cooker; closing the lid starts the cycle); Rice-cooker interaction model (Uses a familiar appliance logic)
rationale: Lift, drop the food in, close: three obvious actions.
judge_comment: The rice-cooker model is familiar and close-to-start is intuitive, but a top-loading microwave raises safety and shielding problems and does not remove the need to choose settings.

title: Wave-Hand Gesture Start
new_elements: Clockwork timer knob (Existing control knob from base_product meta); Proximity gesture sensor (Wave once to start, wave again to stop); Touchless start/stop (Works with messy hands)
rationale: A wave is a universal "go" and "stop" gesture.
judge_comment: Wave start/stop is easy, but it replaces only a button and still needs a timer knob, and accidental triggers are a risk.

title: Same As Last Time Button
new_elements: Clockwork timer knob (Existing knob that must be reset every time); Repeat-last memory button (Replays the previous successful cycle); Habit replay (Same coffee, same result)
rationale: Users repeat routines without having to remember the settings.
judge_comment: A repeat-last button is useful and plausible, but it is a common feature and does little for first-time use.

title: Cup-Detect Drink Shortcut
new_elements: 5-step power knob (Existing power knob from base_product meta); Capacitive shape sensor ring (Recognises the footprint of a mug and applies a drink profile); Automatic drink mode (Drinks are detected without a mode choice)
rationale: The oven adapts to the vessel, so the user doesn't adapt to the oven.
judge_comment: Auto-detecting a mug to apply a drink profile removes mode selection and fits the no-learning-curve need, though capacitive sensing of a mug footprint through a turntable is questionable and the idea only covers drinks.

title: Door-Close-to-Start
new_elements: Door interlock start switch (Replaces the start action and timer wind-up: closing the door starts a default 1-minute cycle, opening it stops.); Start heating by closing door (Uses a gesture people already make, so there is no button to find.)
rationale: Shutting the door is the only instruction, so there is nothing to learn.
judge_comment: Very simple and intuitive, but a fixed 1-minute default offers no control over the cooking result, and it is not very radical (and could start accidentally).

title: Steam-Sniffer Shutoff
new_elements: Humidity sensor in exhaust (Replaces the timer and bell: detects the steam burst that signals the food is heated.); Auto-stop on steam release (Ends the cycle once the food starts steaming.)
rationale: No settings are needed; it simply stops when the food is steaming.
judge_comment: Steam detection is a workable zero-setting stop signal, but it is unreliable for covered or dry foods and the result is imprecise.

title: AI Food-Recognition Camera
new_elements: Cavity vision camera (Replaces the knobs, lamp and window: recognises the food and its portion size.); Auto-program by sight (Sets time and power from what it sees.)
rationale: The machine works out what the food needs so the user doesn't have to.
judge_comment: Camera food recognition removes all input, but it adds cost, struggles with steam and splatter, and is not truly a substitution for simplicity.

title: Talk-to-It Microwave
new_elements: Offline voice module (Replaces the knobs: the user says something like "warm my coffee".); Natural-language control (Runs fully offline, with no app or account.)
rationale: Speech needs no learning at all.
judge_comment: Offline voice control is easy to use but fairly obvious, and noise and ambiguity can cause errors.

title: Wave-to-Start
new_elements: Proximity gesture sensor (Replaces the door button and knob: a hand wave starts or stops heating.); Touch-free control (Useful with greasy or full hands.)
rationale: A wave is an innate gesture that needs no explanation.
judge_comment: Wave-to-start is easy to grasp, but it still needs time and power settings and risks accidental triggering, so it does not remove the learning curve fully.

title: Push-to-Open Door
new_elements: Push-latch door (Replaces the separate release button: press anywhere on the door and it pops open.); Intuitive opening (The whole door acts as the button.)
rationale: There is no hidden button to hunt for.
judge_comment: Push-latch doors already exist and are very feasible, but they only simplify opening, not the rest of the operation.

title: Thermal-Camera Door Display
new_elements: Low-res thermal imager and door screen (Replaces the window mesh and lamp by showing the food in false colour.); See cold spots (Blue means still cold and red means hot.)
rationale: Red and blue for hot and cold is universally understood.
judge_comment: Thermal view of the food is intuitive and useful, though it adds cost and complexity and does not simplify the controls.

title: Shrinking Light Ring
new_elements: LED ring around door (Replaces the dial markings: the ring shrinks as time runs out.); Glanceable progress (Progress can be read from across the room.)
rationale: A shrinking ring needs no numbers or reading.
judge_comment: A shrinking LED ring is an intuitive and feasible progress display, but it only shows output and does not simplify the input side of operation.

title: Elbow-Bump Door
new_elements: Large lower bump pad (Replaces the small release button: bump it with an elbow while holding a plate.); Hands-full opening (The door opens without free hands.)
rationale: It matches what people naturally do when their hands are full.
judge_comment: A hands-free bump door suits real behavior, but it eases opening rather than operation, so it only partly serves the need.

title: Self-Heating Lunchbox
new_elements: Container with built-in RF emitter (Replaces the whole microwave for one portion: the box heats itself when closed and plugged in.); Heat-in-container (Food is heated in the box it is carried in.)
rationale: There is no appliance to learn, only a box.
judge_comment: A self-heating box with its own RF emitter removes the appliance, but it raises serious safety and cost problems and the heating would be uneven.

title: Thermochromic Lid Indicator
new_elements: Colour-changing cover (Replaces reliance on the bell: the lid turns from blue to red when the food is hot.); Visual doneness cue (Shows the food's actual temperature at a glance.)
rationale: Colour shows whether the food is hot without testing it.
judge_comment: A colour-change indicator is feasible and helps with knowing when food is done, but it does not simplify the operation itself and it does not substitute for much.

title: Fridge-Style Magnetic Door
new_elements: Magnetic strip door closure (Pull-to-open magnetic seal replaces the push button, lever and hooks.)
rationale: Everyone already knows how to open a fridge, so the door works without thought and with fewer parts.
judge_comment: A familiar fridge-style pull door makes opening intuitive and simplifies parts, but it leaves the actual cooking controls unchanged and the safety interlock needs care.

title: Hall-Sensor Interlock
new_elements: Sealed Hall-effect door sensors (Contactless magnet sensors that cannot weld shut replace the three microswitches.)
rationale: There are no fiddly switch tolerances that cause 'door won't start' faults confusing users.
judge_comment: This is a sensible reliability substitution, but users barely notice it, so the effect on operational simplicity is indirect.

title: Inverter Supply, No Lethal Cap
new_elements: High-frequency switch-mode HV inverter (A small ferrite inverter replaces the transformer, capacitor and diode doubler.)
rationale: True continuous power levels mean the user never sees odd on/off pulsing, and there is no lethal stored charge.
judge_comment: Inverter supplies are already common in real microwaves, and the benefit is mostly invisible to users, so the contribution to ease of use is weak.

title: Airflow Mode Stirrer
new_elements: Fan-driven metal mode stirrer (A vane spun by the existing cooling-fan airflow scatters microwaves evenly.)
rationale: No turntable to seat, chip or misalign, and any dish shape fits.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are already used in real microwaves, so this is plausible but not new, and it only loosely serves the no-learning-curve need.

title: Frequency-Hop Even Heating
new_elements: RF frequency and phase hopping (A solid-state source sweeps frequency to move hot spots electronically.)
rationale: Food heats evenly with no stirring, turning or user tricks to learn.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF with frequency hopping is real and removes the need for user tricks, but it is costly and replaces the magnetron rather than being a simple substitution.

title: Magnetic Breakaway Cord
new_elements: Magnetic breakaway power connector (The cord snaps off the oven safely if yanked and reconnects in any orientation.)
rationale: Plugging in cannot go wrong and is forgiving for dorm users.
judge_comment: A magnetic breakaway cord is safe and easy to use, but it has little to do with operating the microwave and the power draw raises safety issues.

title: Talk-to-It Control
new_elements: Offline voice command module (Phrases like 'warm my coffee' replace both knobs.)
rationale: Natural speech has zero learning curve.
judge_comment: Voice is intuitive but familiar and not cheaper, and it has issues with accents and noise.

title: Nucleation-Dot Plate
new_elements: Etched nucleation-site glass plate (Micro-etched spots under cups trigger gentle bubbling and prevent superheating.)
rationale: Users get safe drinks without having to learn the 'put a spoon in' rule.
judge_comment: Clever way to remove the superheating safety rule, though it only addresses liquids and the etched plate's effectiveness is uncertain.

title: Susceptor Crisping Floor
new_elements: Ferrite-coated susceptor plate (The plate absorbs microwaves, gets hot and browns the food bottom.)
rationale: Crisp results come with no separate grill mode to learn.
judge_comment: Susceptor plates already exist and mainly add a browning function; the link to no learning curve is weak.

title: Rice-Cooker Top Loader
new_elements: Hinged top lid cavity (Top-loading with a gravity-closed lid, so food sits like in a pot.)
rationale: It uses the familiar pot metaphor, and food cannot spill when the door opens.
judge_comment: The pot metaphor is familiar and avoids spills, but it doesn't change the controls much and top-loading microwave choke and seal design is tricky.

title: Kettle-Whistle Done Signal
new_elements: Steam-powered whistle vent (Steam escaping the cavity blows a whistle when food is hot.)
rationale: A universally understood kettle sound signals readiness with no electronics.
judge_comment: A steam whistle is a charming, intuitive cue, but venting a sealed cavity is hard, may conflict with safety, and works unreliably for dry foods.

title: Solid-State GaN Heart
new_elements: GaN solid-state RF amplifier (Low-voltage (~50 V) transistor RF source replaces the magnetron, HV transformer, diode and capacitor.); GaN RF power module (Compact board-level 2.45 GHz source with digitally set output.)
rationale: With no lethal HV stage, the oven can drop safety warnings and service caveats, and true continuous power makes results predictable without user tuning.
judge_comment: A real substitution of the magnetron, but it mainly addresses cost, safety and power control, and does little to remove the learning curve.

title: Close-Door-to-Cook
new_elements: Door-close start sensor (Closing the door starts sensor-controlled auto cooking.); Starts heating on door closure (The door itself becomes the only control.)
rationale: The door becomes the only interface, so there are zero buttons to learn.
judge_comment: Very simple and feasible, but starting on door close risks accidental runs, and it is not clear what the cook program is.

title: Steam-Sniffer Timer
new_elements: Humidity / steam sensor (Detects the vapour burst released when food is hot.); Stops heating when food is done (Replaces the clockwork timer with a doneness signal.)
rationale: The user never has to guess a duration, because the food decides when it is done.
judge_comment: Sensor-based doneness detection already exists in some ovens, but it directly removes the need to guess a time.

title: Drawer Microwave
new_elements: Slide-out cooking drawer (Push-to-open drawer with choke rim on the drawer front.)
rationale: Everyone already knows how to use a drawer: push to open, push to close.
judge_comment: The drawer is an intuitive, familiar interaction (some drawer microwaves already exist), though the choke design and the substitution are only moderately addressed.

title: Gravity Lid Top-Loader
new_elements: Hinged top lid closed by gravity (Lid weight seats the choke seal; no latch hooks are needed.)
rationale: Lift and drop like a rice cooker, with no button to find.
judge_comment: A top-loading lid that closes by gravity is a fairly radical, simple interaction, but the RF seal and safety interlock need careful design and the food-access ergonomics are questionable.

title: Single Hall-Sensor Interlock
new_elements: Dual-channel Hall-effect door sensor with watchdog (Sealed magnetic sensing replaces three mechanical microswitches.)
rationale: With no worn or misaligned switches, the door always closes and works the same way, so there are no fiddly failures.
judge_comment: Hall-sensor interlocks are very feasible and reliable, but the user-facing simplicity gain is indirect and not radical.

title: Inverter True-Power Supply
new_elements: High-frequency inverter HV supply (Continuously variable magnetron power without duty-cycle cams.)
rationale: Gentle even heating means a single default setting works for all foods, so no power levels need learning.
judge_comment: Inverter supplies already exist in the market and the link to a zero-learning interface is indirect, though the single-default-setting logic is plausible.

title: Susceptor Crisping Floor
new_elements: Ferrite-coated susceptor floor plate (Heats to about 200 °C under microwaves and crisps food from below.)
rationale: Crisp results with no separate grill mode to learn.
judge_comment: Susceptor plates already exist and give crisping without a grill mode, but they only loosely relate to the 'no learning curve' need and are not very radical.

title: Lamp Becomes Grill
new_elements: Quartz-halogen IR browning lamp (Replaces the incandescent light and also browns food during the final seconds automatically.)
rationale: One part gives light and browning with no extra controls.
judge_comment: Combining the light and a browning lamp is a clever substitution that automates browning, though halogen heat and cavity integration are challenging and similar combos already exist.

title: Door Pops at Done
new_elements: Solenoid auto-open door release (Unlatches the door slightly at the end of cooking instead of ringing the bell.)
rationale: An open door means done: an unmistakable visual cue that also vents steam.
judge_comment: Easy to build and a clear done cue, but it only addresses the end of cooking and not how to set or start it.

title: Weighing Floor Auto-Time
new_elements: Load-cell cavity floor (Weighs the food and computes the heating time.)
rationale: Weight replaces guesswork, so timing is automatic.
judge_comment: Weighing removes guesswork, but a load cell in a microwave is tricky and weight alone doesn't determine the right time or power for different foods.

title: Under-Floor Feed
new_elements: Bottom-feed antenna beneath sealed ceramic floor (No exposed waveguide port in the walls.)
rationale: A seamless box with nothing to remove or maintain.
judge_comment: Bottom-feed antenna under a sealed floor is a real design and gives a seamless, nothing-to-maintain interior, though the link to operation simplicity is moderate.

title: LED Fill-Bar Progress
new_elements: LED progress bar on door edge (Fills up as the food heats, replacing the turning-dial reading.)
rationale: A filling bar is universally understood.
judge_comment: An LED bar is easy to understand and simple to build, but it only shows progress and doesn't make starting the microwave any easier.

title: Close-the-Door-to-Start
new_elements: Door closure starts cycle (Shutting the door is the start command, and a default heat program runs.)
rationale: Closing the door is the only action needed, so starting the oven requires no interface at all.
judge_comment: Closing the door to start is very simple and easy to build, but it risks accidental starts, an empty-run hazard, and a fixed program that suits few foods.

title: Inverter Instead of Duty-Cycle Cam
new_elements: Inverter HV supply (Continuously variable power replaces the on/off cam cycling.)
rationale: Gentle, even power by default removes the need to choose a power level for most foods.
judge_comment: Inverter supplies are already in commercial microwaves, and the benefit to simplicity is modest.

title: Magnetic Breakaway Cord
new_elements: Magnetic snap-on power connector (Self-aligning and breakaway, so it cannot be plugged in wrong.)
rationale: The cord simply snaps into place, which is easier than finding an orientation and safer if it is yanked.
judge_comment: Feasible and a safety plus, but plugging in a cord is a one-time action and barely affects day-to-day operation.

title: Phased-Array Beam Steering
new_elements: Multi-antenna phase steering (Moves hot spots electronically instead of rotating the food.)
rationale: There is no turntable to seat, clean or knock off its track, and the food heats evenly anywhere in the cavity.
judge_comment: Removes the turntable and gives even heating without user effort, but phased-array solid-state RF is costly and the idea is not a cheaper substitute.

title: Hall-Sensor Self-Checking Interlock
new_elements: Dual Hall sensors + door magnet (Contactless sensors with a self-test MCU replace three mechanical microswitches.)
rationale: With nothing to wear out or misalign, the door always works without fiddling.
judge_comment: Technically solid substitution, but the user never sees it, so it barely affects learning curve.

title: Auto Rest-Pulse Anti-Superheat
new_elements: Pulsed ending with forced rest (Power is tapered at the end, and the door stays latched 20 s for liquids to settle.)
rationale: The machine builds in safety know-how that users would otherwise have to learn.
judge_comment: Building superheat safety into the cycle removes something the user would have to learn, but the 20 s door lock could frustrate users and it is not clearly a substitution.

title: Susceptor Crisp Tray
new_elements: Ferrite-coated susceptor tray (A passive tray heats up in the microwave field and browns food, replacing a grill element.)
rationale: Crisping happens by using the tray, with no extra mode to understand.
judge_comment: Susceptor trays already exist and mostly add a crisping feature rather than simplify operation.

title: One Knob Does Everything
new_elements: Push-turn encoder knob (Turning sets the time, pushing starts or stops, and power is automatic.)
rationale: A single control removes any question of which knob to use.
judge_comment: Simple and highly usable, but a single dial or knob is already common on microwaves, so it is hardly radical.

title: Just Say It
new_elements: Offline voice command chip (Understands phrases like 'heat my coffee' and 'defrost chicken'.)
rationale: Natural speech is an interface everyone already knows.
judge_comment: Offline voice control is natural and feasible, but voice microwaves already exist and noisy kitchens and phrasing variation add friction.

title: Built-in Splatter Hood
new_elements: Ceiling-hinged glass splatter hood (Drops over the food on closing, replacing loose plate covers.)
rationale: Covering the food happens automatically instead of being a habit the user must learn.
judge_comment: An automatic splatter hood removes a learned habit, but it adds mechanical complexity and does little for operating the controls.

title: Steam-Sniffer Auto Stop
new_elements: Humidity sensor in exhaust duct (Detects the burst of steam released when food is hot and ends the cycle.); Ends cooking when food is hot (Closed-loop stopping replaces open-loop time setting.)
rationale: The machine decides when the food is done, so the user never has to estimate a time.
judge_comment: Sensor-based auto-stop already exists in some microwaves, yet it does fulfil the need; it is moderately specific, though some foods give no steam signal.

title: Talking Done Announcement
new_elements: Voice chip speaker (Says 'Your food is ready, stir and enjoy' instead of ringing a bell.)
rationale: A spoken instruction explains both the outcome and what to do next.
judge_comment: A spoken completion message is easy to understand and cheap to build, but it is an incremental change that only affects the end of the cycle.

title: Thermochromic Ready Plate
new_elements: Colour-change glass tray (Thermochromic enamel turns from blue to red where the food above it is hot.); Reversible thermochromic pigment (Leuco-dye pigment that changes colour at about 60 °C.)
rationale: Red means hot, which is understood by everyone with no learning.
judge_comment: A thermochromic tray gives intuitive heat feedback, but it only shows the result and doesn't simplify operation. It is also cheap to make, though the tray is not a clear substitution.

title: Package Barcode Reader
new_elements: Barcode scanner window (The user holds the ready-meal pack up to the window, and the maker's heating instructions load automatically.)
rationale: The user no longer reads small print on the box or translates it into dial settings.
judge_comment: It removes the need to read instructions for packaged meals, but it needs a database, covers only barcoded food, and similar ideas already exist.

title: Cloche Microwave
new_elements: Lift-off shielded dome (A transparent shielded bell jar lowers over a plate on a heating base, so there is no door at all.)
rationale: Covering a plate is a gesture everyone already knows, so cooking is simply putting the cover on.
judge_comment: Intuitive cover-the-plate gesture removes the door, but a transparent dome that contains microwave radiation and handles steam and heat is hard to make safe.

title: Hall-Sensor Soft Interlock
new_elements: Redundant magnetic Hall-sensor interlock (Contactless sensors with a safety relay detect the door gently, so it doesn't need slamming.)
rationale: A soft close works every time, so users never have to learn the knack of shutting the door firmly enough.
judge_comment: Contactless door sensing removes the need to slam the door, but it's an incremental swap and addresses only a minor usability issue.

title: Roll-Top Shutter Front
new_elements: Tambour metal-slat shutter (Overlapping conductive slats with choke edges roll up like a bread bin lid.)
rationale: A bread-bin motion is familiar, and there is no door swinging into the user.
judge_comment: A roll-top shutter is a radical and familiar interaction, but RF choke sealing on a sliding tambour is hard and the benefit for learning is modest.

title: Fill-Line Tray Markings
new_elements: Etched portion guide tray (Etched circles show 'mug here = 1 click' and 'plate here = 3 clicks', matched to the dial.)
rationale: The instructions live exactly where the food sits, so no manual is needed.
judge_comment: Cheap, intuitive printed guide on the tray that directly removes the need for a manual, though not very radical and the turntable may obscure markings.

title: Smell-Signal Finish
new_elements: Aroma puff cartridge (At the end of the cycle the cam releases a pleasant scent, such as fresh bread, into the room.)
rationale: Smell is an instinctive cue that food is ready, needing no interpretation and no beep to decode.
judge_comment: A scent cue is novel and intuitive, but it only signals the end of the cycle and cartridges need refilling and may annoy users.

title: Plate-Size Auto Program
new_elements: Capacitive footprint sensor floor (Senses the dish diameter and food area to choose the heating time.)
rationale: Whatever the user puts in determines the program, with no input needed.
judge_comment: Automatic program selection removes input entirely, but a capacitive floor cannot reliably sense food type or mass, so heating would be unreliable.

title: Solid-State RF Heart
new_elements: GaN solid-state RF amplifier (Low-voltage semiconductor RF source that replaces the magnetron, voltage doubler and HV diode.)
rationale: Precise, continuous power control lets a single button give consistently good results.
judge_comment: A solid-state RF source is a real technology shift, but it is expensive and only loosely tied to the no-learning-curve need.

title: Stirrer Fan Instead of Turntable
new_elements: Air-driven mode stirrer (Metal vanes in the ceiling, spun by the cooling-fan airflow, spread the field evenly.)
rationale: With no turntable, any dish of any size goes anywhere in the cavity and nothing jams.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are well known and removing the turntable cuts a small friction point, but the gain in operational simplicity is modest.

title: Magnetic Latchless Door
new_elements: Magnetic door catch (Fridge-style magnets hold the door shut, so a simple pull opens it and no push button is needed.)
rationale: Pulling a door open is universally intuitive, so there is no button to find.
judge_comment: Pull-to-open is very intuitive, but magnets alone may not meet door-seal and interlock safety requirements, and the idea is not radical.

title: Ferrite Gasket Door Seal
new_elements: Ferrite-loaded silicone gasket (Absorbs leakage RF, replacing the precision quarter-wave choke rim.)
rationale: A soft, wipe-clean seal works even if the door is slammed or knocked out of alignment.
judge_comment: Ferrite-loaded gaskets are plausible and tolerant of misalignment, but they have little effect on ease of operation.

title: Transparent Conductive Door
new_elements: ITO-coated glass door (Transparent conductive film blocks microwaves without a perforated metal screen.)
rationale: A clear view of the food lets users judge doneness by eye, with no learning.
judge_comment: ITO glass could give a clear view of the food, but it is hard to make it block microwaves reliably, and the view only indirectly helps with operation.

title: Thermochromic Turntable
new_elements: Colour-changing glass tray (Shifts from blue to red as the food above it gets hot.); Shows food temperature visually (Replaces guesswork and touch-testing.)
rationale: Red means hot, which everyone understands.
judge_comment: Colour feedback is intuitive and useful, but a glass tray in a microwave cannot accurately show the temperature of the food above it, and the tray surface heats unevenly.

title: Fibreglass-PTFE Waveguide Cover
new_elements: PTFE-coated glass-fibre sheet (Non-stick, wipeable replacement for brittle mica.)
rationale: Nothing to maintain or replace; a quick wipe is enough.
judge_comment: PTFE-coated fibreglass is a real, practical replacement for mica, but it is maintenance-related and barely touches the learning curve.

title: Susceptor Crisp Plate
new_elements: Ferrite-susceptor glass plate (The turntable absorbs microwaves and becomes a hot browning surface.)
rationale: Crisp food with no extra mode to learn, because the plate just does it.
judge_comment: Susceptor plates exist and give browning with no extra mode, but this serves ease of use only moderately and is not very novel.

title: Glowing Choke Rim
new_elements: LED strip in choke rim (Replaces the 25 W incandescent lamp and changes colour with cooking progress.)
rationale: Progress is shown by light colour, so there is no display to read.
judge_comment: A sensible LED substitution that gives intuitive progress feedback, though it does not simplify the controls and the colour mapping needs some interpretation.

title: Door-Wound Turntable
new_elements: Spring drive wound by door closing (Closing the door winds a spring that turns the tray, replacing the turntable motor.)
rationale: Fewer electrical parts, and it works without any thought from the user.
judge_comment: A clever mechanical substitute for the motor, but the spring would only run briefly and it does little for the user's operating experience.

title: Drawer-Bowl Microwave
new_elements: Pull-out drawer cavity (A drawer replaces the hinged door; you drop the food in and push it shut.)
rationale: Everyone knows how to use a drawer.
judge_comment: Microwave drawers exist, and a drawer is intuitive, but the door was never the hard part of operating it, so the gain is modest.

title: Shelf-Height Power Select
new_elements: Two-level field-tuned shelves (The top shelf is full power and the bottom shelf is defrost, using the field distribution instead of a power knob.)
rationale: Where you put the food is the setting.
judge_comment: Using shelf position as the power setting is a clever way to remove the knob, but making stable field zones with reliable power differences is hard.

title: Talking-Dot Plates
new_elements: IR-readable temperature dot on dishware (The oven reads the dot through the window to track the plate's temperature.)
rationale: Accurate stopping with no user input.
judge_comment: Zero-input stopping is highly relevant, but it needs special dishware, and an IR dot is unlikely to read through the window and steam reliably.

title: Visual Done Pulse
new_elements: Room-visible pulsing light plus soft chime (Replaces the bell with signals that are both seen and heard.)
rationale: 'Done' is unmistakable, even for hard-of-hearing users.
judge_comment: An easy, practical accessibility improvement to the done signal, but it is incremental and only touches a small part of operation.

title: Energy-Counting Timer
new_elements: Delivered-energy dose meter (Counts energy delivered rather than seconds, so 'one cup' always means the same heating.)
rationale: Settings are labelled in food portions, not abstract minutes.
judge_comment: Portion-based settings could remove the need to guess times, but measuring delivered energy to match food portions is imprecise, and it does not replace a part with something cheaper.

title: Food-Icon Dial
new_elements: Pictogram timer dial (Dial positions show a cup, plate, soup bowl and frozen block instead of minutes.)
rationale: Users point at what they are heating instead of estimating minutes.
judge_comment: Pictogram dials are intuitive, but the mapping from icon to time is vague and the idea is not very radical.

title: Mug-Shaped Recess Switch
new_elements: Beverage cup cradle microswitch (Setting a mug in the cradle auto-selects 90 s.)
rationale: The most common task needs no input at all.
judge_comment: A mug-detecting cradle removes input for the common task, but it is unreliable across mug types and doesn't cover other tasks.

title: Braille-Notched Knob
new_elements: Tactile detent knob with raised markers (Clicks and bumps mark 1, 2 and 5 min.)
rationale: Elderly users with poor eyesight can set it by feel.
judge_comment: Tactile detent knobs are easy to build and help some users, but the idea is incremental rather than radical.

title: Steam Whistle End Signal
new_elements: Kettle-whistle exhaust vent (A vent whistles when cavity steam rises, replacing the bell.)
rationale: A whistling kettle needs no explanation.
judge_comment: A whistle is an intuitive end signal, but it is unreliable because microwaved food does not always produce steam, and it only replaces the bell.

title: Thermochromic Plate
new_elements: Colour-changing turntable plate (The glass turns red where the food is hot.)
rationale: Users see 'done' as a colour rather than guessing.
judge_comment: Intuitive visual doneness cue is appealing, but thermochromic glass in a microwave that heats unevenly and cycles often is questionable, and it does not replace any control.

title: Grandma Mode Fixed Program
new_elements: Single 'Warm my meal' button (A fixed 2 min program at 70 % power.)
rationale: One button does the one thing most elderly users need.
judge_comment: Very simple and easy to use, but a one-button fixed program is an obvious idea and is not radical, and one fixed setting won't suit many foods.

title: Light-Bar Countdown Lamp
new_elements: Cam-driven segmented light strip (The strip dims segment by segment as time elapses.)
rationale: Time left is shown from across the room.
judge_comment: A segmented light bar shows remaining time clearly from a distance, but it only displays time and does not simplify operation.

title: Voice-Bell Recorded Message
new_elements: Recordable end-chime module (A family member records 'Your food is ready, Mum'.)
rationale: A familiar voice explains itself, with nothing to decode.
judge_comment: A recordable chime is easy to build and friendly, but it only affects the end alert and does little for operating the appliance.

title: Defrost Dome Instead of Power Knob
new_elements: Partially perforated metal defrost dome (Placing the dome over food passively cuts absorbed power to about 30 %.); Passive partial shielding for field attenuation (Aperture sizing sets the fraction of microwave energy reaching the food.)
rationale: 'Cover it to defrost' is a physical, memorable rule that replaces a cryptic power scale.
judge_comment: A passive shield is a clever replacement for power levels, but metal in a microwave risks arcing and gives unpredictable attenuation.

title: Magnetic Pull Door
new_elements: Magnetic catch with reed interlock (A fridge-style magnet holds the door; reed switches provide the interlock.); Permanent-magnet catch and reed-switch sensing (Replaces hook-and-lever latch mechanics.)
rationale: It opens like a fridge, an action everyone already knows.
judge_comment: A familiar fridge-style opening with a clear magnet and reed-switch design, but it addresses only the door and is not radical.

title: Tap-Count Timer
new_elements: Ratchet button adding 30 s per press (Each press winds the timer cam forward by 30 s.)
rationale: Counting presses is simpler than aiming at a tiny scale on a dial.
judge_comment: Press-counting is intuitive and easy to build with a ratchet cam, but it is a modest tweak rather than a radical idea.

title: Logarithmic Timer Scale
new_elements: Log-scale cam timer dial (Half the dial covers 0-2 min, giving precise short times.)
rationale: The most common short reheats become easy and accurate to set without fiddling.
judge_comment: A log scale gives finer control over short times, but a nonlinear dial may confuse some users, so it only partly serves a no-learning-curve goal.

title: Shrinking Ribbon Countdown
new_elements: Red ribbon window driven by timer shaft (A coloured band visibly shrinks as time runs out.)
rationale: Remaining time is seen at a glance from across the room, with no numbers to read.
judge_comment: Intuitive visual countdown that is simple to build, but it does not simplify setting the time.

title: Kettle-Style Toggle
new_elements: Single rocker with bimetal auto-off (Flip on; a cavity bimetal flips it off when steam is detected.)
rationale: It works exactly like a kettle, an appliance everyone already knows.
judge_comment: The kettle metaphor is familiar, but steam-triggered bimetal cut-off is unreliable for solid foods and the mechanism is loosely defined.

title: Servings Dial
new_elements: Dial marked in mugs and plates (Positions read 1 mug, 2 mugs, 1 plate and so on, rather than minutes.)
rationale: The units match the user's mental model of what they are heating.
judge_comment: Dial units in mugs and plates match mental models and are simple to build, but food variability makes results imprecise and the idea is not very radical.

title: Spring-Steel Flex Hinge
new_elements: Stamped spring-steel flexure hinge (A single-piece hinge that also self-closes the door.)
rationale: The door closes itself, so users cannot leave it ajar and then wonder why nothing works.
judge_comment: A self-closing flexure hinge is plausible and removes a common failure, though it only addresses one small part of operation and is not very radical.

title: Traffic-Light Disc
new_elements: Red-amber-green rotating disc behind window (Driven by the timer shaft; shows green when done.)
rationale: Traffic-light colours are understood universally, with no reading needed.
judge_comment: A timer-driven color disc is cheap and easy to build and understand, but it only communicates status and does not simplify input.

title: Whole-Panel Door Opener
