new_elements: Full-height pressure bar release (Pressing anywhere on a tall front bar opens the door, even with an elbow.)
rationale: There is no small target to find, so the door opens even with full hands.
judge_comment: Easy door opening helps usability, but it addresses only one interaction and is not very radical.

title: Bimetal Turntable Hub Cut-Off
new_elements: Thermostat disc in turntable hub (Heat conducted from the plate opens the circuit at about 70 °C.)
rationale: It provides automatic stopping without the user having to judge a time.
judge_comment: A bimetal cut-off removes the need to judge time, but plate temperature is a poor proxy for heating state, and it fails with cold or dry loads and varied foods.

title: Language-Free Pictogram Fascia
new_elements: Embossed pictogram control fascia (A tactile, wordless panel that is the same in every region.)
rationale: Tactile icons can be understood by touch and sight in any language.
judge_comment: Embossed pictograms are easy to build and help universal understanding, but they are incremental and not very radical.

title: Self-Closing Sloped Hinge
new_elements: Rising-butt hinge with gravity close (The helical hinge lifts the door as it opens, so its weight swings it shut.)
rationale: The door always ends up closed and ready to run.
judge_comment: A rising-butt hinge is a simple and workable substitute that closes the door by gravity, but it only loosely addresses operating simplicity.

title: Close-the-Door-to-Cook
new_elements: Door-closure start sensor (Closing the door starts a default reheat cycle and opening it stops the cycle.); Starts heating on door closure (Uses the interlock state as the user interface.)
rationale: The only action is the one the user already performs: put food in and shut the door.
judge_comment: Zero-step operation is appealing, but safety concerns and accidental heating (e.g., empty or unsuitable items) limit it, and it substitutes the start button rather than a part.

title: Fridge-Style Magnetic Door
new_elements: Magnetic door strip with pull handle (Replaces the push-release latch lever with a fridge-like magnetic closure.)
rationale: Opening becomes a natural pull, with no hidden button to find.
judge_comment: A pull-handle magnetic door is simple and feasible, but it is incremental and has a modest effect on learning curve.

title: Hall-Sensor Interlocks
new_elements: Redundant Hall-effect door sensors (Contactless magnets replace the three microswitches and cannot weld shut.)
rationale: Removes mechanical misalignment failures, so the door simply always works.
judge_comment: Hall sensors improve reliability rather than ease of use, so they barely address the need.

title: Nucleation-Etched Turntable
new_elements: Laser-etched boiling-seed glass plate (Micro-pits under cups prevent superheating.)
rationale: Removes a hidden danger that users would otherwise need to learn about.
judge_comment: Nucleation-etched glass is a clever substitution for the plate, but it addresses a safety hazard more than operation simplicity, and its effectiveness is uncertain.

title: Metal Detector Cutoff
new_elements: Inductive metal sensor coil under floor (Refuses to start and blinks red if metal is present.)
rationale: Users need not know the 'no metal' rule because the oven enforces it.
judge_comment: A metal detector enforces the no-metal rule without learning, but the sensing is hard to do reliably inside a microwave cavity and the idea is fairly incremental.

title: Sealed Ceramic Waveguide Window
new_elements: Glazed alumina waveguide window (A wipe-clean ceramic replaces the flaking, burning mica sheet.)
rationale: No consumable part for users to learn to inspect or replace.
judge_comment: A ceramic waveguide cover is a sound part swap, but it mostly affects maintenance and has little to do with operating simplicity.

title: Plate-Down Start
new_elements: Pressure-sensing floor switch (Will not run empty; runs only when a dish is present and the door is shut.)
rationale: Prevents the empty-run mistake without any instruction.
judge_comment: A floor pressure switch prevents empty runs and removes a hidden mistake, though it is an incremental safety feature and may misread light dishes.

title: Wave-to-Extend
new_elements: Top-mounted IR proximity sensor (Waving a hand over the top adds 30 s.)
rationale: Touchless and obvious, it also works with messy hands.
judge_comment: Wave-to-add-time is intuitive and touchless, but it only covers time extension, not the whole operation, and risks accidental triggers.

title: Magnetic Breakaway Cord
new_elements: MagSafe-style appliance connector (Detaches if yanked instead of pulling the oven off the counter.)
rationale: Accidents are absorbed by design.
judge_comment: A magnetic breakaway cord is a feasible, proven safety idea, but it is largely unrelated to ease of operation.

title: Food Picture Dial
new_elements: Pictogram dial face (Replaces numeric timer markings with printed food icons (mug, plate, popcorn).); Select by recognizing food (Users turn the dial to a picture instead of minutes.); Numeric minutes require prior knowledge (Users must know cook times.)
rationale: Pictures are universally understood, and this costs only ink.
judge_comment: It is cheap and easy to build, but pictogram dials already exist and the idea is not very radical.

title: Natural Talk Control
new_elements: Offline speech recognition (A small-vocabulary on-chip voice model.); Microphone module (Replaces the knobs; understands commands like 'warm my coffee'.); Conversational command (Plain speech sets the program.)
rationale: Speaking is a skill everyone already has.
judge_comment: Voice control is natural, but it is a common idea, and kitchen noise and the need to know the commands limit it.

title: Colour-Coded Bowls Replace Power Knob
new_elements: Colour-sensing floor (Replaces the 5-step power cam; red bowl means high, blue bowl means defrost.); Power by container colour (Colour maps to duty cycle.); Abstract power levels (Users don't know what 'level 3' means.)
rationale: Users grab the 'defrost bowl' instead of decoding power levels.
judge_comment: Selecting power by bowl color is intuitive and playful, but color sensing inside a microwave cavity is unreliable and it locks users into specific bowls.

title: Drawer That Starts Itself
new_elements: Microwave drawer (Replaces the hinged door and push-release button; closing the drawer starts heating.); Close-to-start (The close action doubles as the start action.); Door release button plus separate start (Multiple discrete actions are needed.)
rationale: Push food in and it heats; that is the whole procedure.
judge_comment: Close-to-start collapses the procedure into a single action, but the start time or power still has to come from somewhere, and microwave drawers already exist.

title: Flatbed Mode Stirrer
new_elements: Hidden mode-stirrer fan (Replaces the glass turntable and motor with a metal fan in the waveguide that scatters energy.); Even heating without rotation (Spreads field patterns evenly.); Turntable must be seated correctly (An off-track plate jams; the glass breaks or goes missing.)
rationale: There are no loose parts to place correctly; any dish anywhere works.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are already common and remove the turntable placement step, but the idea is incremental and its listed elements are partly contradictory.

title: Daylight Light Pipe
new_elements: Top light-pipe window (Replaces the 25 W incandescent lamp with a shielded skylight that channels room light inside.); Passive interior illumination (Lights the cavity with no bulb to fail.); Waveguide-below-cutoff optics (Small-diameter tubes block microwaves but pass light.)
rationale: There is no bulb to replace, so users never face a dark mystery box.
judge_comment: Clever passive lighting that removes a bulb, but it barely affects operational simplicity and room light may be too dim inside.

title: Fixed-Power Inverter
new_elements: Inverter magnetron drive (Continuous variable power.); Auto-power controller (Replaces the 5-step power knob; picks power from sensed load.); Eliminate power choice (Users never set power.)
rationale: It removes an entire control users rarely understand.
judge_comment: Inverter with auto power removes a confusing control and is plausible, but inverter microwaves already exist and load sensing is vaguely defined.

title: Kitchen-Wide Status Halo
new_elements: LED halo ring (Replaces the single bell; glows amber while heating and green when ready.); Ambient status communication (Visible from across the room.); One-shot bell easily missed (A single ding is often not heard.)
rationale: Traffic-light colours need zero explanation.
judge_comment: A simple LED status halo is easy and intuitive, but it is an incremental feedback improvement rather than a radical one.

title: Keep-Warm Instead of Alarm
new_elements: Low-duty hold cycle (Replaces the end bell's urgency with gentle warming until the door opens.); Food waits for user (No reheating needed.); Duty-cycle control (Reuses the power-cam logic electronically.)
rationale: Users never have to react or re-operate the machine.
judge_comment: Keep-warm hold removes the need to react to the end signal, though it risks overcooking and food safety issues.

title: Spring-Wound Turntable
new_elements: Door-wound turntable spring (Replaces the turntable motor; closing the door winds a spring that rotates the plate.); Rotation without motor (Cheaper and silent.); Clockwork energy storage (Shares the escapement with the timer.)
rationale: Users get even heating automatically from a gesture they already make.
judge_comment: A clever motor-free turntable, but it barely affects operational simplicity, and a door-wound spring is mechanically awkward.

title: Hourglass Sand Timer
new_elements: Flip-over sand timer interlock (Replaces the clockwork timer; flipping a sealed hourglass holder closes the circuit until the sand runs out.); Visible tangible timing (Users see time pass.); Tilt-switch control (A mercury-free ball tilt switch reads the hourglass orientation and weight.)
rationale: Hourglasses are a universally understood time metaphor.
judge_comment: A flip-over hourglass interlock is intuitive and wild, but its fixed durations are imprecise and the tilt-switch mechanism is muddled.

title: Knee-Bump Start Bar
new_elements: Front bumper switch (Replaces the start/knob action with a bar along the bottom edge; bump to add 30 s.); Body-operated control (No fingers needed.); Knobs need free hands and grip (Hard with full hands or arthritis.)
rationale: It's the crudest possible interface, which means nothing to learn.
judge_comment: A bump bar is simple and accessible, but accidental activation is a risk and it only adds time in 30 s steps.

title: Self-Opening Steam Vent Door
new_elements: Bimetal door unlatch (Replaces the timer end mechanism and bell; a bimetal strip heated by exhaust steam pops the latch.); Passive heat-triggered finish (No electronics; the door cracks open when hot.); Bimetallic actuation (Thermostat-style snap disc.)
rationale: An open door plainly says 'done' at near-zero cost.
judge_comment: A passive bimetal door pop-open signals completion cheaply, but it doesn't address how to set the cooking, and an unexpectedly opening door is a safety and consistency concern.

title: Shadow-Puppet Food Projection
new_elements: LED backlit silhouette projector (Replaces the incandescent lamp; projects a food silhouette and progress onto the wall or counter.); Ambient progress display (A large, glanceable image.); Low-power LED projection (Gobo-style optic.)
rationale: Large pictorial feedback requires no reading.
judge_comment: A large pictorial progress projection is easy to understand, but it only provides output feedback and adds cost and complexity instead of simplifying operation.

title: No-Controls Sensor Box
new_elements: Fused sensor brain (Replaces all knobs, the bell and the button; weight, IR and steam sensing decide everything.); Zero-input heating (Close the door and it heats correctly.); Sensor fusion firmware (A cheap MCU combines the three sensors.)
rationale: No controls means no learning curve by definition.
judge_comment: A zero-input microwave fully removes the learning curve, but reliably sensing food and deciding heating from weight, IR and steam is technically difficult and the idea is fairly obvious.

title: Air-Driven Stirrer
new_elements: Wind-turbine stirrer driven by cooling airflow (Exhaust air from the cooling fan spins the mode stirrer, removing the turntable motor.)
rationale: Even heating with one fewer moving part means no tray placement for the user to learn.
judge_comment: A cleverly cheap air-driven stirrer replaces a motor, but the user-facing simplicity gain is minimal and airflow in a cavity is tricky.

title: Cloche Dome Microwave
new_elements: Lift-off shielded cloche dome (Mesh-glass dome lowered over a base plate; dome contact closes the interlocks.)
rationale: Covering a plate is a gesture everyone already knows, so there are no doors or hinges to work out.
judge_comment: Covering a plate with a dome is intuitive, but a mesh-glass dome with RF containment and interlocks is awkward and the control problem remains.

title: Talking Ready Voice
new_elements: Voice chip saying 'Ready - stir and enjoy' (ISD-style playback chip replaces the bell and also gives next-step advice.)
rationale: The oven tells the user in plain words what to do next.
judge_comment: A voice chip is easy to build and slightly helpful, but it does little for operating the oven, which is the real learning hurdle.

title: Light-Pipe Illumination
new_elements: External LED feeding a cavity light pipe (LED outside the cavity shines through a sub-wavelength hole via an acrylic rod.)
rationale: The light never burns out, so users never face a dark oven and a confusing bulb replacement.
judge_comment: A light pipe fed by an external LED is plausible and concrete, but it barely affects ease of operation.

title: Drop-In Liner Bowl
new_elements: One-piece removable glass-ceramic cavity liner (Microwave-transparent tub lining floor and walls; lift out and dishwash.)
rationale: Cleaning becomes 'lift it out, wash it', with no wiping technique to learn.
judge_comment: A removable microwave-transparent liner simplifies cleaning but is about maintenance rather than operation, and sealing and cavity-tuning concerns make it harder than it looks.

title: Pop-Up Done Flag
new_elements: Spring pop-up flag on top of cabinet (Cam releases a bright flag at end of cycle, like a turkey timer, visible from across the room.)
rationale: The done signal stays visible after the moment passes, so a missed ding no longer means cold food.
judge_comment: A mechanical done flag is cheap and concrete, but it addresses the end-of-cycle signal rather than operation.

title: Knock-to-Add-Time
new_elements: Piezo knock sensor in top panel (Each knock on the cabinet adds 30 s; two quick knocks cancel.)
rationale: Any surface is a button, and knocking works even with wet or full hands.
judge_comment: Knock input is easy with full hands and technically simple, but it is not obvious to users at first and risks accidental triggers and mis-timing.

title: Fridge-Style Magnetic Door
new_elements: Magnetic gasket door with conductive elastomer seal (Pull to open, swing shut; a conductive rubber gasket plus choke rim replaces the latch hooks.)
rationale: It works exactly like the fridge door the user opens every day.
judge_comment: Familiar fridge-style door is intuitive, but microwave leakage and seal reliability make it a modest gain; the conductive gasket is a concrete substitution.

title: Bump Bar Door Release
new_elements: Full-width bump bar (Panic-bar style strip along the door edge; pushing it anywhere releases the latch.)
rationale: Arthritic hands or full hands can open the door with an elbow.
judge_comment: A bump bar makes opening easy and accessible, but opening was rarely the main learning hurdle, so the benefit is modest.

title: Whistling Lid
new_elements: Microwave-safe whistling cover (Kettle-like reed in a plastic food cover whistles when food steams.)
rationale: The kettle metaphor tells users 'it's hot now' with zero learning.
judge_comment: A whistling lid uses an intuitive kettle cue, but it does not simplify setting the controls and is only a partial solution.

title: Three Big Minute Buttons
new_elements: 1-2-3 minute piano keys (Three large mechanical keys that latch the matching cam start position.)
rationale: Three obvious choices cover most real reheating jobs with zero ambiguity.
judge_comment: Three obvious choices are easy to use and mechanically plausible, though fixed minutes limit flexibility and the idea is not very radical.

title: Wind-Up Timer
new_elements: Spring escapement timer (Egg-timer clockwork that needs no synchronous motor.)
rationale: It works like the familiar egg timer and gives one global SKU at a lower cost.
judge_comment: A familiar egg-timer interface is intuitive and cheap, but it's a retro approach with limited precision and no new capability.

title: Roll-Top Tambour
new_elements: Metal slat roll-top door (Bread-bin style tambour of overlapping steel slats with choke edges.)
rationale: Everyone knows how a bread bin opens, so no button or latch is needed.
judge_comment: A familiar bread-bin tambour is intuitive to open, but sealing microwave leakage around slats is very hard, and the door's ease of use is only part of the operation.

title: Shrinking Light Ring
new_elements: LED ring countdown bezel (A ring of lights around the knob that goes out segment by segment.)
rationale: Remaining time is visible from across the room without reading numbers.
judge_comment: Easy to implement and helpful for glanceable time, but it addresses feedback rather than operation, and LED countdown rings are already fairly common.

title: Spring-Steel Band Hinge
new_elements: Integral flexure hinge (A spring-steel strip stamped in one piece with the door, self-closing.)
rationale: A door that gently self-closes removes the 'forgot to shut it' failure.
judge_comment: A self-closing flexure hinge is concrete and prevents a common user error, but the spring-steel strip is a doubtful fit for a heavy door with a safety interlock.

title: Inclined Self-Closing Door
new_elements: Rising-butt gravity hinges (Helical hinges lift the door slightly when opened, so gravity swings it shut.)
rationale: The door closes itself, so starting a cycle never fails silently.
judge_comment: Rising-butt hinges are a proven, cheap mechanism that makes the door close itself, though the idea is only moderately novel and helps operation only a little.

title: Hourglass Front
new_elements: Flip-hourglass timer switch (Flip a sealed sand glass mounted on a pivot; its weight shift trips the power switch when empty.)
rationale: The oldest timer in history is universally understood.
judge_comment: An hourglass is universally understood, but a fixed duration and a mechanical trip switch make it imprecise and awkward, and it substitutes the timer with something no simpler.

title: Thermochromic Ready Plate
new_elements: Thermochromic glaze turntable (The tray rim turns from blue to red when the food above it is hot.)
rationale: The colour itself shows that the food is ready, so there is nothing to interpret.
judge_comment: Colour feedback is intuitive, but the tray shows its own temperature rather than the food's, and it only helps after the start, not with operation.

title: Shrinking Light Ring
new_elements: LED countdown halo (A ring around the door window shrinks as time runs out, like a pie chart.)
rationale: Remaining time is visible at a glance without reading numbers.
judge_comment: Easy to read and easy to build, but it only displays the time and doesn't simplify operating the oven.

title: Fridge-Magnet Door
new_elements: Magnetic door closure (Ferrite strip magnets hold the door shut with no latch hooks; the interlock uses a Hall sensor.)
rationale: It is pushed shut and pulled open like a fridge, so there is no latch to work out.
judge_comment: A fridge-style magnetic closure is easy to understand, but microwave safety interlock requirements and magnet strength make it harder to implement.

title: Talking Ding
new_elements: Voice chip announcer (Says 'Your food is ready, careful, it's hot.')
rationale: A spoken message needs no decoding of beeps.
judge_comment: Spoken end-of-cycle message is easy to understand and cheap, but it is a common feature and covers only one part of operation.

title: GaN Power Module
new_elements: GaN solid-state RF amplifier (Low-voltage DC source replacing the magnetron and the HV chain.)
rationale: Continuous power means the user never has to think about power levels.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF is a genuine substitution of the magnetron and removes power-level fiddling in principle, but the link to simple operation is indirect and cost is high.

title: Countertop Buzz
new_elements: Foot haptic vibrator (Vibrates the counter and table when the food is done.)
rationale: Deaf users get feedback through touch, which needs no learning.
judge_comment: Haptic done-alert is intuitive and inclusive, but it serves accessibility more than operational simplicity and is not much of a substitute for the beep.

title: Ceiling Glow Alert
new_elements: Upward LED projector (Floods the kitchen ceiling warm orange when the food is ready.)
rationale: The alert is visible from anywhere in the room.
judge_comment: Room-wide ceiling glow is easy to understand and feasible, but it is a modest feedback improvement that doesn't simplify operating the oven.

title: Anti-Eruption Floor
new_elements: Nucleation-textured tray spot (A micro-rough ring under the cup position transfers vibration to seed bubbles.)
rationale: Users need no knowledge of superheating to stay safe.
judge_comment: A nucleation-textured spot to prevent superheating is a clever passive safeguard, but its effectiveness is doubtful since vibration from a tray doesn't reliably seed bubbles.

title: Reed-Switch Interlocks
new_elements: Redundant Hall/reed door sensors (Contactless sensing with no slam needed to engage.)
rationale: A gentle close always works, so there is no 'slam it harder' trick to learn.
judge_comment: Contactless door sensing is plausible and removes a small annoyance, but it barely affects operating simplicity and is not radical.

title: Thermochromic Mug Ring
new_elements: Thermochromic cavity floor ring (Changes colour when the liquid placed on it is near boiling.)
rationale: A colour signal warns of superheated liquid without any instruction.
judge_comment: An instruction-free visual warning is clever, but it concerns safety rather than operation, and a floor ring gauging liquid temperature is unreliable.

title: Susceptor Ceramic Floor
new_elements: Ferrite-loaded ceramic floor plate (Absorbs microwaves, heats up and crisps the underside of food.)
rationale: Food crisps automatically with no separate crisp mode to learn.
judge_comment: Ferrite susceptor floor is workable and removes a crisp mode, though susceptor plates already exist and it is a modest simplification.

title: Built-In Boiling Stone
new_elements: Porous ceramic nucleation stud in mugs (Provides bubble sites so liquids cannot superheat.)
rationale: Eruptive boiling is prevented physically, so there is no safety rule to learn.
judge_comment: A nucleation stud is a plausible, concrete safety substitute, but it only addresses superheating and does little for operational simplicity.

title: Phased-Array Beam Steering
new_elements: Multi-antenna phase steering (Electronically sweeps hot spots across the food in place of a turntable.)
rationale: Food heats evenly without users needing to stir or rotate it.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF phased arrays are real and replace the turntable, but cost and complexity are high and the benefit to learning curve is indirect.

title: Door-Wound Spring Turntable
new_elements: Clockwork spring wound by door closure (Closing the door winds a spring that turns the plate.)
rationale: The turntable turns with no motor and no user action.
judge_comment: A clockwork turntable is simple and plausible, but a motor is already cheap and the user never operates the turntable anyway.

title: Thermal Camera Leftover Recognition
new_elements: Low-res thermal imager (Detects cold spots and redirects heating until the whole dish is warm.)
rationale: Users never have to restart cooking because of a cold middle.
judge_comment: Automatic, even heating would remove the need to learn settings, but a thermal imager inside a microwave cavity is costly and technically hard, and it is not a substitution.

title: Frequency-Agile Metal Tolerance
new_elements: Adaptive-frequency impedance matching (Shifts frequency to avoid arcing field peaks around metal.)
rationale: A forgotten spoon does not cause drama.
judge_comment: Metal tolerance removes a major rule users must learn, but solid-state frequency-agile RF is costly and arcing is hard to eliminate fully.

title: Unbreakable Silicone Floor Mat
new_elements: Removable silicone mat (Replaces the glass turntable; dishwasher-safe and unbreakable.)
rationale: There is no fragile part to align or break.
judge_comment: A silicone mat removes alignment and breakage worries and is simple, but it loses the rotating function, which hurts even heating, and silicone may deform with heat.

title: Clamshell Top-Loader
new_elements: Gravity-closed hinged lid (The lid's weight seals the choke, so no latch is needed.)
rationale: Lift and drop like a waffle iron, the most intuitive opening there is.
judge_comment: A gravity-closed top-loading lid replaces the latch and door in an intuitive way, but microwave leakage and safety interlock requirements make it questionable.

title: Auto-Eject Tray Instead of Bell
new_elements: End-of-cycle bell (Base-product component being substituted); Motorised presenting tray (Slides the food out toward the user when it is ready); Signal that food is ready by physically presenting it (An unambiguous end state)
rationale: Food arriving in front of the user cannot be misread the way a bell or beep can.
judge_comment: Presenting the food physically is an unambiguous end signal, but a motorised ejecting tray adds cost and spill risk, and it is not really a cheaper substitute.

title: Mode-Stirrer Fan Replaces Turntable
new_elements: Glass turntable (Base-product component being substituted); Metal mode-stirrer blade (A rotating reflector in the cavity roof that scatters microwaves evenly); Heat evenly with no rotating plate (Flat floor, no parts to seat)
rationale: There is no plate to misalign, jam, or bump large dishes against, so it just works.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are an established technology, and the benefit to ease of use is only marginal because turntables are already effortless.

title: Pull Handle Instead of Push Button
new_elements: Door push-release button (Base-product component being substituted); Magnetic catch door with grip handle (Opens like a fridge door); Open the door with an obvious affordance (The handle shows how to open it)
rationale: A handle visibly invites pulling, so no one has to hunt for a release button.
judge_comment: Pull handles are already common and highly feasible, and they give a small affordance gain, but the idea is not radical.

title: Bell-Jar Dome Microwave
new_elements: Box cavity with door (Base-product component being substituted); Liftable ITO-coated glass dome (A transparent shielded cloche placed over the plate on a base); Cover food to heat it (A placing-a-lid metaphor)
rationale: Putting a cover over a plate is an intuitive action that needs no instruction.
judge_comment: The cloche metaphor is intuitive, but a large conductive-glass dome needs a reliable RF seal at the base and is awkward and costly.

title: Light-Pipe Skylight
new_elements: 20-25 W incandescent interior lamp (Base-product component being substituted); Waveguide-below-cutoff light pipe (Channels room light into the cavity through narrow tubes that block microwaves); Illuminate the cavity with zero energy (Passive lighting)
rationale: There is no bulb to replace or fail, and the food is always visible.
judge_comment: Passive sub-cutoff light pipes are clever and plausible, but they don't make operation any simpler, and the light would be dim.

title: Thermochromic Cavity Walls
new_elements: 20-25 W incandescent interior lamp (Base-product component being substituted); Thermochromic enamel liner (Cavity walls glow warm colours near hot food); Ambient heat-status display (The whole interior acts as the indicator)
rationale: Heat is shown as colour, which every user understands without instruction.
judge_comment: Color as a heat indicator is intuitive, but thermochromic enamel on cavity walls is impractical because the walls stay cool and the coating would not hold up, and it doesn't replace the lamp's function.

title: Spoken Request Control
new_elements: Timer and power knobs (Base-product components being substituted); Offline voice-command chip (Understands phrases such as 'warm my coffee'); Natural-language operation (Talk to it like a person)
rationale: Speech is the interface everyone already knows.
judge_comment: Voice is intuitive, but it is already common in smart microwaves and is noisy and less reliable than a knob; it is not cheaper or simpler.

title: Burn-Smell Guardian
new_elements: User supervision (The implicit human 'component' being substituted); Metal-oxide gas sensor (Detects scorching VOCs and cuts power); Prevent burning automatically (Built-in safety net)
rationale: Mistakes cannot become disasters, so novices can use it with confidence.
judge_comment: Gas sensing for scorching exists in some ovens and helps novices avoid disasters, but it addresses mistakes rather than the operation learning curve directly.

title: Smart Plate Thermometer
new_elements: Glass turntable (Base-product component being substituted); RF-harvesting sensor plate (A ceramic plate with an embedded thermometer that tells the oven when the food is done); Contact-measured doneness (Accurate stop point)
rationale: The plate decides when the food is hot, so the user does nothing.
judge_comment: Auto-stop by plate sensing removes user decisions, but an RF-harvesting thermometer in a microwave field is hard, and it doesn't replace the turntable's function.

title: Gesture Wave Start
new_elements: Timer knob start action (Base-product function being substituted); IR proximity gesture sensor (Wave a hand to start, wave again to stop); Touch-free operation (Works even with messy hands)
rationale: A single wave is the simplest possible human command.
judge_comment: Wave-to-start is simple in principle, but accidental triggers and the lack of any way to set time or power limit how much it helps.

title: Fridge Label Printer Link
new_elements: Timer and power knobs (Base-product components being substituted); QR leftover labels (Printed when food is stored; the microwave scans the label and reheats correctly); Leftovers carry their own reheating recipe (Closes the kitchen loop)
rationale: Whoever eats the leftovers needs no knowledge of how to reheat them.
judge_comment: QR labels remove the need to set the microwave, but depend on a separate printer ecosystem and a user habit, so the fit with a simple no-learning product is partial.

title: Bell Replaced by Phone-Free Wearable Buzz
new_elements: End-of-cycle bell (Base-product component being substituted); Clip-on vibrating fob (Buzzes in your pocket when the food is ready, like a restaurant pager); Notify the user anywhere in the home (Familiar pager metaphor)
rationale: Everyone knows the restaurant buzzer, and it needs no app setup.
judge_comment: A simple pager fob is feasible and familiar but only addresses end-of-cycle notification, not core operation, and is fairly obvious.

title: Weigh-and-Go Turntable
new_elements: Spring-scale turntable timer (Food weight compresses a spring under the turntable, which mechanically sets the cook time.); Sets duration from food mass ()
rationale: The user just puts the food in and the machine decides the time, so nothing needs setting.
judge_comment: Auto-setting time from weight needs no input, but weight is a poor proxy for cook time, and the spring mechanism would be inaccurate and the turntable would interfere.

title: Top-Loading Lid
new_elements: Gravity-closed top lid (Lift the lid like a rice cooker; its weight closes and seals it.)
rationale: It reuses the familiar pot-lid gesture, needs no latch, and gives a clear view down into the food.
judge_comment: A familiar rice-cooker lid gesture and no latch simplify operation, but top-loading is awkward for a microwave and sealing against leakage is a concern.

title: Elbow/Knee Door Paddle
new_elements: Large lower-front push paddle (A wide paddle releases the latch with an elbow, knee or hip when the hands are full.)
rationale: Users can open the door while holding a plate, without hunting for a small button.
judge_comment: Easy and practical hands-free opening, but it only addresses the door and not the learning curve of operation.

title: Defrost Dome Instead of Power Knob
new_elements: Partially shielded mesh defrost dome (A passive cover that blocks about 70% of the energy to give gentle heating.)
rationale: Users 'set' low power by putting a lid on the food, a physical action rather than an abstract setting.
judge_comment: A passive shielded dome is a clever substitution for a power setting, but a mesh dome that blocks about 70% of the energy is tricky to build safely, and the dome's effect on heating is hard to predict.

title: Shrinking Light Ring
new_elements: LED countdown ring around the knob (A lit arc shrinks as time passes and the whole ring flashes green when done.)
rationale: Users read how much time is left from across the room without deciphering a dial scale.
judge_comment: An LED ring is easy to read, but it adds cost and is a display tweak rather than a substitution that simplifies operation.

title: Auto-Open Door at Finish
new_elements: Timer-triggered latch release (The cam end-stop kicks the latch lever and the door gently pops ajar.)
rationale: The finished food is presented to the user with no button to press.
judge_comment: An auto-opening door removes a step and uses a simple mechanism, though it could be a safety or annoyance concern and does not address setting the time.

title: Wave-to-Start
new_elements: IR proximity gesture sensor (A wave of the hand starts a standard reheat; another wave adds time.)
rationale: There is no fine motor control or button reading involved.
judge_comment: Wave-to-start is easy to use, but it is not discoverable, can trigger accidentally, and is a poor fit for adding time.

title: Glow Status Instead of Window
new_elements: Solid door with colour status glow (There is no window; the door edge glows amber while heating and green when done.)
rationale: Traffic-light colours communicate status instantly, and the solid door is cheaper and better shielded.
judge_comment: The color status glow is intuitive, but removing the window cuts visibility of the food and adds LEDs, which undermines the cost saving.

title: Tactile Peg Timer
new_elements: Braille and peg-board timer face (Raised notches every 30 s with a firm click.)
rationale: Blind and low-vision users can set the time by touch alone.
judge_comment: A tactile peg dial is very feasible and accessible, but it is close to an ordinary mechanical dial and still requires setting a time.

title: Calendar Meal Wheel
new_elements: Caregiver-set weekly program wheel (A rotating wheel preloaded with meal settings by day; the user presses one button.)
rationale: Users with cognitive decline only need to press 'Today'.
judge_comment: A caregiver-preset wheel with a single 'Today' button nearly eliminates learning for a niche group, but it requires setup and limits flexibility.

title: Close-the-Door-to-Cook
new_elements: Door closure starts cycle (Shutting the door starts heating and opening it stops heating, with no start button.)
rationale: The door, an action users already perform, becomes the only control.
judge_comment: Door-close start is intuitive, but it has no way to set duration and invites accidental starts and safety concerns.

title: Hall-Sensor Interlocks
new_elements: Redundant Hall-effect door sensing (Contactless magnetic sensors cannot weld shut, replacing the mechanical microswitches.)
rationale: The door closes with no precise click needed and has fewer failure modes to confuse users.
judge_comment: Technically sound substitution, but it's an invisible internal change that barely affects operation or learning curve.

title: Talking Ready Chime
new_elements: Voice prompt chip (Says 'Food ready, careful it's hot' instead of ringing a bell.)
rationale: Plain-language feedback removes the need to interpret beeps.
judge_comment: Easy and helpful for clarity, but it only addresses the end feedback and is a fairly incremental idea.

title: Flat Ceramic Floor
new_elements: Fixed glazed ceramic floor (A flush wipeable floor replaces the removable glass turntable and roller ring.)
rationale: There is nothing to reassemble after washing.
judge_comment: A fixed ceramic floor eliminates the turntable and reassembly mistakes, though it may compromise even heating.

title: Repeat-Last Paddle
new_elements: Single 'same again' paddle (Replays the last cycle, covering the daily coffee reheat.)
rationale: Routine use takes one tap with no setting.
judge_comment: Very simple and feasible but only covers repeat use and the first use still needs setup.

title: Color-Coded Dishes
new_elements: Optical base reader plus colored dishes (A red bowl means soup and a blue plate means a meal, and the oven reads the color.)
rationale: Choosing a dish is choosing a program.
judge_comment: Color-reading dishes make program choice tangible, but require proprietary dishes and limit flexibility.

title: Door-Wound Turntable
new_elements: Door-closing spring motor (Closing the door winds a spring that turns the turntable, replacing the electric motor.)
rationale: It uses fewer electrics and stays silent and self-evident.
judge_comment: A spring motor wound by the door is a clever substitution, but it does little for ease of operation and the turntable would likely run unevenly.

title: Hip-Bump Door Release
new_elements: Full-width bump bar (Push anywhere on the lower front with a hip or elbow to open.)
rationale: It opens hands-free with no small button to find.
judge_comment: A hands-free bump-bar release is easy to use and feasible, but it addresses only door opening and not the operating controls.

title: Rotating Drum Cavity
new_elements: Revolving drum chamber (The opening rotates away from the waveguide, making RF physically impossible when open.)
rationale: One turning motion loads, seals, and starts, with safety guaranteed by geometry.
judge_comment: A rotating drum cavity is a radical idea with intuitive loading, but sealing, size and cost make it hard, and it does not substitute a cheaper part.

title: Color-Change Safe Mug
new_elements: Thermochromic etched-bottom mug (Etched nucleation sites prevent superheating, and ink turns red when too hot.)
rationale: Safety is built into the cup, not into the user's knowledge.
judge_comment: Safety-focused and plausible, but it is a mug rather than a change to how the microwave is operated, so it only loosely serves the need.

title: Steam-Sniffer Auto Stop
new_elements: Exhaust humidity sensor (Detects the steam burst that signals the food is hot.); Stop when food is ready (Ends heating based on the food's state rather than a guessed time.)
rationale: No need to know how long anything takes.
judge_comment: Humidity sensor cooking already exists in premium microwaves, and it is practical, but it is still not radical.

title: Package Barcode Reader
new_elements: Door-mounted barcode scanner (Reads ready-meal barcodes and loads the manufacturer's heating profile.); Cloud or embedded food-profile database (Maps product codes to power and time sequences.); Program from packaging (Replaces reading and transcribing on-pack instructions.)
rationale: Showing the box to the oven is the whole interface.
judge_comment: Scanning is easy for ready meals, but it needs a database, covers only packaged food, and is useless for leftovers.

title: Talk To It
new_elements: Offline voice module (Understands phrases like "warm my coffee" or "defrost bread".); Natural-language control (Replaces all physical controls.)
rationale: Users just say what they want.
judge_comment: Voice control is easy to use but it is not simpler or cheaper, and it fails in noise, with accents, and for users who do not know what to say.

title: Pull-Handle Door
new_elements: Magnetic-catch pull handle (Opens like a fridge door, with no release button to find.); Intuitive door opening (Matches existing appliance habits.)
rationale: Pulling a handle is self-evident.
judge_comment: A pull handle is intuitive and cheap, yet many microwaves already use one, and it does nothing for the rest of the operation.

title: Hold-Pressure Door
new_elements: Force-sensing door panel (A short tap gives 30 s; holding the push longer adds more time.); Duration by touch (The door itself is the controller.)
rationale: There is no panel to read at all.
judge_comment: Using the door as the controller is a bold idea, but hold-to-add-time is not discoverable and gives no feedback, so it may in fact create a learning curve.

title: Probe Skewer
new_elements: Microwave-safe fibre-optic probe (Stick it in the food; heating stops at the target core temperature.); Core-temperature termination (Guarantees food is hot all the way through.)
rationale: Stick it in and wait, with no guessing.
judge_comment: Core-temperature probes exist and remove guesswork, but the user must still insert the probe and a fibre-optic probe adds cost and hygiene work, so it does not fully remove the learning curve.

title: Wave to Heat
new_elements: Front proximity/gesture sensor (Each hand wave adds time; a palm held up stops the oven.); Touch-free control (Works with greasy or full hands.)
rationale: Wave for more and hold up a palm to stop are natural gestures.
judge_comment: Proximity sensing is cheap and plausible, but wave counts and hidden gestures must be learned, and it replaces buttons without making them simpler.

title: Routine Learner
new_elements: Clock-aware usage learner (Pre-selects the morning coffee or lunch reheat based on time of day.); Anticipatory presets (The right setting is usually already selected.)
rationale: The machine learns the user, instead of the user learning the machine.
judge_comment: Reduces the need for user input through adaptation, though the learning mechanism is vague and may guess wrong.

title: Knee-Bump Door
new_elements: Lower-front bump plate (Bump with a hip or knee to open when hands are full.); Hands-full access (Replaces the finger-press release button.)
rationale: Opening is effortless and obvious in real kitchen moments.
judge_comment: A knee-bump opener is obvious and practical for full hands, though accidental opening and its tie to the operating-simplicity need are limited.

title: Shrinking Light Bar
new_elements: Door-edge LED progress bar (The bar shrinks as time runs out.); Glanceable progress (Replaces reading a small knob position.)
rationale: Progress bars are universally understood.
judge_comment: Easy to build and intuitive for showing progress, but it only displays status and does little to simplify setting up the operation.

title: Magnetron Feels the Food
new_elements: Anode-current load monitor (Infers when the food has heated from changes in the magnetron's load.); Sensorless doneness (Requires no extra sensor hardware.)
rationale: It delivers automatic operation cheaply, with no user input.
judge_comment: Using magnetron load to infer doneness is clever and cheap, but the signal is likely too noisy and varies too much between foods to be reliable.

title: Hourglass Window
new_elements: Liquid-crystal hourglass on door (Shows animated sand draining as the time remaining.); Metaphorical countdown (Replaces the dial scale with an archetypal symbol.)
rationale: Everyone reads an hourglass instantly.
judge_comment: An hourglass display makes time remaining intuitive and is feasible, but it only addresses reading the countdown, not setting or operating the microwave.

title: Steam-Sniffer Auto-Stop
new_elements: Exhaust humidity sensor (Sensor in the vent air ends the cycle when steam surges from the food.)
rationale: The oven decides when food is hot, so the user does not need to guess a duration.
judge_comment: Humidity sensing is a known feature on premium models, though it does remove the need to guess a time.

title: Push-to-Open Door
new_elements: Push-push touch latch door (Pushing anywhere on the door releases it, like a kitchen cabinet.)
rationale: There is no button to locate, which helps users with poor sight or full hands.
judge_comment: Push-latch doors are proven and easy to use, but they only simplify opening, and the rest of the interface still has to be learned.

title: Fridge-Style Magnetic Door
new_elements: Magnetic catch with reed-switch interlocks (The door is held by a magnet strip; reed switches sense closure.)
rationale: The user just pulls the door like a fridge, so there is no latch to work out.
judge_comment: A magnetic door is familiar and plausible with reed interlocks, but the safety interlock and RF sealing need care, and the gain over a standard latch is small.

title: Talking End Alert
new_elements: Voice-chip announcer (Says 'Ready – it's hot, stir before eating' instead of ringing a bell.)
rationale: The appliance explains itself in plain words.
judge_comment: A voice announcer is cheap and clear, but it only affects the end of the cycle and talking appliances already exist.

title: Inverter Auto-Gentle
new_elements: Switch-mode inverter HV supply (Light inverter with continuous power modulation chosen automatically from load sensing.)
rationale: The power knob disappears because the supply adapts to the food itself.
judge_comment: Inverter supplies exist, but sensing the load to auto-pick power is hard; it does remove the power knob.

title: Frozen-Detect Auto Defrost
new_elements: Detects frozen state and switches to defrost (An IR reading below 0 °C triggers low-duty cycling automatically.)
rationale: Nobody needs to know which mode defrosts.
judge_comment: Automatic defrost detection removes the need to choose a mode, but IR only reads the surface, so accuracy is limited.

title: Nucleation Mug Spot
new_elements: Etched boiling-chip zone in the cup holder (A marked ring for mugs, plus an included ceramic stir stick that seeds bubbles.)
rationale: Superheating safety is built in instead of being something to learn.
judge_comment: A passive nucleation aid builds in safety without learning, but users still need to use the stick and the ring placement is of uncertain effect.

title: Color-Coded Power Knob
new_elements: Blue/amber/red color-zone power knob (Colors replace wattage numbers: blue = defrost, amber = soften, red = hot.)
rationale: Colors are understood instantly, unlike '440 W'.
judge_comment: Easy and clear for power, but time still needs setting and the idea is incremental rather than radical.

title: Shelf-Height Power
new_elements: Labeled shield shelf insert (Placing food under a perforated shield shelf gives gentle defrost power passively.)
rationale: Users choose power by where they put the food, not by turning a dial.
judge_comment: Passive power selection by shelf height is a clever substitution for a dial, but shielding behavior is hard to make predictable and users must learn what the heights mean.

title: Steam-Sense Auto Stop
new_elements: Exhaust steam bimetal sensor (Bimetal disc in the exhaust duct snaps when steam temperature rises, ending the cycle); Detects food readiness from released steam (Closed-loop stop condition)
rationale: The user just presses start and the oven decides when the food is hot.
judge_comment: Steam-triggered stop gives a true one-touch experience, but a bimetal disc is unreliable across foods that produce little steam, and the idea is a known sensor-cook approach.

title: Glass-Box Microwave
new_elements: ITO-coated transparent cavity walls (Conductive transparent oxide film on glass shields RF while showing the whole cavity); Transparent conductive oxide shielding (Thin metal-oxide film reflects 2.45 GHz while staying optically clear)
rationale: Users see the food from any angle with no lamp, so they never wonder what is happening inside.
judge_comment: Transparent conductive shielding is plausible and novel, but it does little for ease of operation and adds cost.

title: Tray-Free Mode Stirrer
new_elements: Roof-mounted metal mode stirrer (Slowly rotating metal fan blade that scatters the field; the cavity floor is flat); Field mode stirring (Rotating reflector constantly reshuffles standing-wave patterns)
rationale: There is no tray to seat, lose or break, and any dish fits anywhere.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers already exist and removing the tray is a small convenience that does little for operation without a learning curve.

title: Speaking Chime
new_elements: Voice-chip end announcer (Says 'Your food is ready, careful, it's hot')
rationale: Plain-language feedback removes any need to interpret beeps.
judge_comment: Easy and helpful for feedback, but it only covers the end of the cycle and talking appliances are already familiar.

title: Shape-Coded Tactile Controls
new_elements: Raised-relief tactile fascia (Embossed snowflake, cup and flame shapes at each knob detent)
rationale: Controls explain themselves by touch and shape, without printed labels.
judge_comment: Embossed icons aid intuitive use and accessibility but are a modest change that still depends on a conventional control set.

title: Flat Glass-Ceramic Floor
new_elements: Sealed glass-ceramic cavity floor (A flat, wipe-clean floor with bottom-fed RF through a sealed window replaces the tray, roller ring and mica patch)
rationale: Removing loose parts leaves nothing to assemble or misplace.
judge_comment: A flat sealed floor removes loose parts and is plausible, but it only indirectly supports operational simplicity.

title: Pop-Up Done Flag
new_elements: Spring-loaded pop-up flag (A bright flag pops out of the top at end of cycle, like a turkey timer or mailbox flag)
rationale: Done-ness is visible across the room and stays visible until noticed.
judge_comment: A mechanical done flag is an intuitive signal, but it addresses only the end-of-cycle moment and adds a moving part.

title: Projected Guidance
new_elements: Pico-projector hint light (Projects 'Place food here', then 'Turn knob', onto the counter or door glass)
rationale: The appliance teaches itself in context, so no manual is needed.
judge_comment: Contextual projected prompts reduce the learning curve, but a pico-projector is more complex and costly than the controls it replaces, so it fits SUBSTITUTE only loosely.

title: Fan-Hum as Feedback
new_elements: Tuned chime fan blade (The fan produces a gentle tone that rises as time runs out)
rationale: Progress can be heard without looking, so there is nothing to read.
judge_comment: Audible progress through the fan tone is clever and cheap, but fan pitch is hard to tune and does not simplify input.

title: One Knob To Rule Them All
new_elements: Single combined time-power dial (One cam whose inner sectors set low power for defrosting and whose outer sectors set full power for reheating.)
rationale: Merging two controls into one removes the need to work out how time and power interact.
judge_comment: A single combined dial reduces controls but still requires the user to understand the settings, so it is incremental.

title: Thermochromic Tray
new_elements: Thermochromic glaze turntable (The tray glaze turns from blue to red as the food sitting on it heats up.)
rationale: Users read doneness by colour, an intuitive cue that needs no explanation.
judge_comment: Colour cue is intuitive, but the tray heats indirectly and thermochromic glazes in a microwave are unreliable and don't indicate true food doneness.

title: Continuous Power, No Power Knob
new_elements: GaN solid-state amplifier with auto power (Smoothly modulated output follows the absorbed power, so power never needs to be chosen.)
rationale: Removing the power control removes one decision the user could get wrong.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF with auto power is real and removes one setting, but it replaces the magnetron rather than a user-facing complexity, and users still need to set time.

title: Shelf-Height Power
new_elements: Two-level rack: gentle top, strong bottom (Cavity geometry gives a weaker field on the upper shelf for defrosting and melting.)
rationale: Where you put the food sets the power, which is a physical cue rather than a setting.
judge_comment: Placement as a physical cue for power is intuitive, but engineering stable field gradients in a cavity is difficult and unreliable.

title: Just Say It
new_elements: Offline voice command module (Understands phrases such as 'warm my coffee' or 'defrost chicken'.)
rationale: Natural speech is the zero-learning interface.
judge_comment: Offline voice control is feasible and needs no learning, but it is a common idea and not a substitution of a part for something simpler.

title: Glow Ring Ready Signal
new_elements: Exterior LED halo ring (The ring is amber while heating and green when ready, and is visible across the room.)
rationale: Traffic-light colours are understood instantly.
judge_comment: Easy to understand and build, but it adds a status signal rather than substituting a part, and it only marginally reduces the learning curve.

title: Feel-It Fascia
new_elements: Tactile raised-symbol fascia (Embossed icons and Braille dots replace printed labels.)
rationale: Controls can be understood by touch, which suits blind and elderly users.
judge_comment: Tactile icons help accessibility and are easy to make, but they only change the labels and not the operating logic.

title: Frozen Detector Auto-Defrost
new_elements: IR sensor that detects sub-zero food (Automatically switches to defrost cycling when the food is frozen.)
rationale: Users never need to know that defrosting requires a lower power.
judge_comment: Removes the need to know defrost power levels, but IR sensing of frozen food through the cavity is imperfect and it adds cost rather than substituting something simpler.

title: Dark Means Done
new_elements: Light and motion stop to signal completion (The light goes out and the tray stops, so the bell is deleted.)
rationale: It uses natural, self-evident state cues and cuts a part.
judge_comment: Removing the bell is simple, but a light-off cue is weak and easy to miss, and many microwaves already do this, so it may not work as well as the bell.

title: Weight-Set Timer
new_elements: Spring scale under turntable driving the timer cam (Heavier food deflects the scale further, which sets a longer time automatically.)
rationale: Putting food in sets the time, so the user never has to estimate minutes.
judge_comment: Weight-based timing is clever and fully automatic, but weight correlates poorly with cooking time and the spring scale is hard to make accurate.

title: Countdown Light Bar
new_elements: LED bar on the door that shrinks as time passes (Replaces both the interior lamp and the timer dial reading.)
rationale: A shrinking bar shows progress with no need to read a dial.
judge_comment: A shrinking light bar is easy to understand and cheap, but it addresses feedback rather than input, so it only partly serves the need.

title: Pop-Open Finish
new_elements: Spring that pops the door ajar at end of cycle (The timer cam releases the latch instead of only ringing a bell.); Signals completion visibly and physically (Useful for users who cannot hear the bell.)
rationale: An open door plainly means the food is ready.
judge_comment: A spring-open door gives clear physical completion feedback and is simple, but it does not help with setting up the cook.

title: Revolving Drum Cavity
new_elements: Rotating cylindrical cavity with one opening (User turns the drum so the opening faces forward to load, then back to seal it.)
rationale: It is open or closed with nothing in between, so it cannot be misused.
judge_comment: Radical rotating cavity is clear in concept, but sealing, loading spills and the awkward geometry make it impractical.

title: Steam Sniffer Auto-Stop
new_elements: Humidity sensor in exhaust (Detects the burst of steam released when food is hot.); Stop when food is hot (Ends heating based on food state rather than elapsed time.)
rationale: Heating stops when the food is ready, so the user never has to predict a time.
judge_comment: Steam and humidity sensing already exists in sensor-cook models, and it is less reliable for foods that don't steam, so this substitution is not new.

title: Hidden Mode Stirrer
new_elements: Ceiling mode stirrer fan (A rotating metal fan behind the cavity ceiling spreads the microwaves evenly; it replaces the glass turntable.); Even heating with no moving tray (Removes the plate that has to be seated and the dish that can catch and stop rotating.)
rationale: Without a tray to place correctly or clean, there is nothing to get wrong.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are already common in microwaves, and removing the turntable only slightly helps ease of use without addressing the controls.

title: Push-to-Open Door
new_elements: Touch-latch door (Pushing anywhere on the door pops it open, like a kitchen cabinet.); Open without finding a button (Works with an elbow while hands are full.)
rationale: The whole door is the control, so there is no button to look for.
judge_comment: Push-to-open doors are easy and practical but they already exist and only affect one part of the interaction.

title: Pop-Open When Done
new_elements: Solenoid door kicker (Unlatches the door at the end of the cycle; it replaces the bell.); Physical done signal (An open door clearly means the food is ready.)
rationale: It works like a toaster popping up, which nobody needs to learn.
judge_comment: Simple and cheap and it does replace the bell, but it only addresses the end of the cycle, not setting up the operation.

title: Thermal-Eye Auto-Stop
new_elements: Thermopile array sensor (Reads the food surface temperature without contact.); Heat to target temperature (Stops at a temperature that is good to eat.)
rationale: Asking the oven to make food hot, rather than run for N minutes, removes any need for judgement.
judge_comment: Targeting temperature removes guesswork, but surface-only IR sensing is inaccurate and the sensor is more expensive than a timer, so it is not a true substitute.

title: Smell-Sensing Doneness
new_elements: VOC gas sensor (Detects cooking aromas and the onset of scorching.); Odour-based auto stop (Ends the cycle before food burns.)
rationale: Burning is prevented automatically, so mistakes cannot happen.
judge_comment: Auto-stop from a VOC sensor removes the need to set time, though the sensor is not very reliable and the idea doesn't say how the cycle starts.

title: Toaster Lever
new_elements: Spring lever switch (Pushing the lever down starts the oven; it springs up when the sensor says the food is done.); Familiar toaster metaphor (Replaces the timer and bell.)
rationale: It borrows a gesture people have used all their lives.
judge_comment: The toaster-lever metaphor is intuitive, but reliable sensing of doneness in a microwave is hard, and the idea does not say how the sensor works.

title: Talking Countdown
new_elements: Voice prompt speaker (Announces 'one minute left' and 'ready, careful, hot'.); Spoken feedback (Replaces the bell and serves blind users.)
rationale: Plain speech is clearer than an ambiguous ding.
judge_comment: Voice prompts make feedback clearer and help blind users, but they do not simplify setting up the oven, and talking appliances already exist.

title: Hourglass Window
new_elements: Rotating hourglass door insert (Flipping it starts the oven, and the oven runs until the sand has run through.); Visible time remaining (Uses a universal symbol for time.)
rationale: Everyone can read an hourglass.
judge_comment: An intuitive time metaphor, but a rotating hourglass in a shielded door is hard to build, and one fixed duration is inflexible.

title: Repeat-Last Button
new_elements: Memory 'Again' button (Repeats the last time and power used.); Habit replay (Replaces re-dialling the same settings.)
rationale: Daily routines take one press.
judge_comment: Useful one-press shortcut for repeat use, but common on existing microwaves, not radical, and does nothing for first-time users.

title: Flat Wipe Floor
new_elements: Flat glass-ceramic floor (A seamless base with a hidden rotating antenna; it replaces the turntable and roller ring.); Nothing to reassemble (Cleaning is just a wipe.)
rationale: No loose parts means no wrong assembly.
judge_comment: Flat glass floor with a hidden antenna is a realistic substitution that removes parts, but it addresses cleaning more than operation learning.

title: Haptic Food Detents
new_elements: Detent knob with food clicks (Stronger clicks mark common foods along the dial.); Feel-based selection (Lets users find a setting without looking.)
rationale: Users find the right setting by touch alone.
judge_comment: Food-specific click detents help eyes-free use, but users must learn which click maps to which food.

title: Done-Light Beacon
new_elements: Top-mounted ring light (Pulses green until the door is opened, so the user never forgets food inside.); Persistent done reminder (Replaces the single bell ring.)
rationale: The signal stays visible until the user acts on it.
judge_comment: A persistent light is easy and helpful, but it only addresses the done signal, not operation, and it is not radical.

title: Fill-Bar Progress Strip
new_elements: LED progress bar (Empties as cooking proceeds, replacing the creeping knob pointer.); Progress at a glance (Shows how much of the cycle remains.)
rationale: It reads like a phone battery bar, which everyone recognises.
judge_comment: A familiar battery-style progress bar is easy to read and cheap, but it is incremental and does not simplify setting the cook.

title: Phone-Free Fridge Magnet Remote
new_elements: Magnetic recipe tiles (Tiles stuck on the oven's side panel select programs by position, like a menu board.); Rearrangeable household presets (Families arrange tiles for their usual foods.)
rationale: Each household shapes the controls into its own simple menu.
judge_comment: Magnetic position-based tiles are a creative, tangible menu, but sensing tile positions adds complexity and some setup learning.

title: Transparent Shielded Dome
new_elements: Interior incandescent lamp + perforated door (Base viewing parts being substituted.); ITO-coated glass cloche housing (Fully see-through RF shield that room light passes through.); Transparent conductive oxide shielding (Indium tin oxide film blocks 2.45 GHz while staying optically clear.)
rationale: Users can see their food at all times, so checking progress needs no thought.
judge_comment: ITO-shielded see-through dome is radical, but it is costly, may leak at 2.45 GHz, and only loosely serves simple operation.

title: Doneness Color Halo
new_elements: End-of-cycle bell (Base audible alert being substituted.); RGB LED ring (Glows red while cooking, amber near done and green when ready.)
rationale: Traffic-light colors are understood instantly from across the room.
judge_comment: A color status ring is easy and clear, but it adds to the bell rather than substituting it, and it does little for the main operation.

title: Solid-State Beam Steering
new_elements: Magnetron + glass turntable (Base heating source and rotating plate being substituted.); GaN RF emitter array (Phase-steered emitters heat evenly with no moving plate.); Solid-state RF cooking (Gallium nitride amplifiers with closed-loop power control.)
rationale: No plate to seat, wash or align, and no cold spots to work around.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF is real and removes the plate, but it is costly and only indirectly cuts the learning curve.

title: Hidden Mode Stirrer
new_elements: Glass turntable (Base rotating plate being substituted.); Ceiling metal mode-stirrer fan (Scatters the field so a flat floor heats evenly.)
rationale: Any dish, put anywhere, just works.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are already common and plausible, but they have only a modest effect on operation simplicity.

title: Reflected-Power Sensing
new_elements: User time selection (Base manual input being substituted.); Waveguide reflected-power detector (Infers load and doneness from RF reflection with no added sensor in the food.)
rationale: Automatic sizing of the cycle at negligible added cost.
judge_comment: Automatic cooking with no input fits the need well, but inferring doneness from reflected RF is technically unreliable and the idea is vague on how it works.

title: Smart-Glass Peek Door
new_elements: Lamp + mesh window (Base viewing parts being substituted.); PDLC switchable door over shield film (Turns clear when touched, frosted otherwise.)
rationale: Touch to see inside; no bulb to change.
judge_comment: Switchable glass is a striking swap for the lamp and window, but it only marginally helps operation simplicity and adds cost and RF shielding complexity.

title: Hourglass Display
new_elements: Dial pointer (Base time indicator being substituted.); Animated sand LED panel (Shows remaining time as falling sand.)
rationale: An hourglass is a universal symbol for time remaining.
judge_comment: An hourglass animation is easily understood and cheap to implement, but it only improves the time display and is incremental.

title: Defrost Ice Sensor
new_elements: Low-power knob step for defrost (Base defrost method being substituted.); Dielectric change detector (Automatically switches to defrost mode when it detects frozen food.)
rationale: Users never need to know that a defrost mode exists.
judge_comment: Automatic defrost detection removes a mode users would otherwise need to learn, but reliably sensing frozen food by dielectric change is technically hard.

title: Red-Wedge Visual Timer
new_elements: Shrinking red-disc timer face (A coloured disc wedge on the cam shaft visibly shrinks as time runs out.)
rationale: Remaining time can be read at a glance without reading any numbers.
judge_comment: A shrinking wedge gives an intuitive visual of remaining time with a simple mechanical mechanism, but it only helps with reading time and not with setting it.

title: Turntable Clock Face
new_elements: Tray rim time markings with fixed pointer (The 5 rpm tray rim carries marks, and the user sets a number of turns instead of minutes.)
rationale: Time becomes something you can see happening on the food itself.
judge_comment: Setting time as turns of the tray is a quirky, visible idea, but the tray's slow speed and variable rotation make timing imprecise and the concept less intuitive.

title: Three Word Buttons
new_elements: Warm / Thaw / Melt latching buttons (Three large mechanical buttons select duty-cycle cams in place of five numbered steps.)
rationale: Users choose an intent in plain words rather than an abstract power percentage.
judge_comment: Plain-word intent buttons with cams are simple and plausible, but similar presets already exist and the approach is not radical.

title: Twist-the-Handle Control
new_elements: Rotary door handle timer (Pull the handle to open the door, and twist it to set the time.)
rationale: All interaction happens in one place the hand already touches.
judge_comment: Combining open and time-set in the handle is intuitive and simple, but the mechanical integration is tricky and the idea is only moderately novel.

title: Cloche Lid Oven
new_elements: Lift-off shielded cloche dome (A transparent conductive dome lowers onto a choke-sealed base plate, with no hinges or latch.)
rationale: Covering a plate is the most natural possible action.
judge_comment: Lowering a dome over the food is highly natural, but a latchless conductive dome with an RF choke seal poses serious safety and leakage problems.

title: Wave-Hand Gesture Start
new_elements: IR proximity gesture pad (One wave adds 30 s, and holding a hand over the pad stops cooking.)
rationale: It works with messy hands and has no buttons to decode.
judge_comment: The gesture pad is easy to build and works with messy hands, but gestures have to be learned and it can trigger accidentally.

title: Knee-Bump Door Bar
new_elements: Full-width lower push bar (A bump with an elbow, knee or plate edge anywhere on the bar opens the door.)
rationale: There is no small target to find when both hands are full.
judge_comment: Easy door opening helps usability but covers only one small part of operation, and the substitution is modest.

title: No-Charge Capacitorless Inverter
new_elements: High-frequency switch-mode inverter with active discharge (A small-film-cap inverter that empties itself within milliseconds.)
rationale: True continuous power levels remove the confusing on/off pulsing, so results match what users expect.
judge_comment: Inverter tech is real and gives continuous power, but the benefit is largely invisible to users and the 'no-charge' claim is vague.

title: Phased-Array Beam Steering
new_elements: Multi-antenna RF phase steering (Electronically moves hot spots across the food.); Even heating without motion (Removes cold spots without any moving parts.)
rationale: Food comes out evenly hot, so the user never has to learn to 'stir halfway'.
judge_comment: Beam steering with phased antennas is novel and removes stirring, but it is complex and expensive for a household oven.

title: Warm / Hot / Boil Target Dial
new_elements: Sets target food temperature (Replaces power level with the outcome the user actually wants.)
rationale: Choosing an outcome is intuitive, whereas choosing a wattage needs learning.
judge_comment: Outcome-based dial is intuitive, but microwaves cannot easily sense food temperature without an IR sensor or probe, and the idea names no mechanism.

title: Ferrite Elastomer Gasket
new_elements: RF-absorbing ferrite silicone gasket (Absorbs leakage even when the rim is dirty.)
rationale: No precise door care is needed; it just works.
judge_comment: Ferrite-loaded gaskets are plausible and sturdy, but they address leakage and maintenance rather than operating simplicity.

title: Wax Phase-Change Heat Guard
new_elements: Paraffin phase-change heat sink (Absorbs heat spikes and passively caps the RF source temperature.)
rationale: There are no nuisance trips that confuse users; the oven simply keeps working.
judge_comment: A paraffin heat sink could avoid nuisance trips, but its link to ease of use is indirect and its capacity for sustained microwave heat load is doubtful.

title: Nucleation-Etched Turntable
new_elements: Micro-etched nucleation glass plate (Textured spots seed bubbles in cups placed on top.)
rationale: Users never need to know about superheating rules.
judge_comment: A nucleation-etched plate is a clever passive safety measure, but it has little to do with ease of operation and its effectiveness is uncertain.

title: Turntable-Motor Magnetic Stirrer
new_elements: Magnet coupling under plate with stir bar (Reuses the turntable motor to spin a PTFE stir bar in liquids.)
rationale: Drinks come out evenly hot and safe with no stirring step.
judge_comment: Clever reuse of the turntable motor, but the user must place a stir bar and it only addresses liquids, so it does little for learning-curve simplicity.

title: Self-Resetting PTC Fuse
new_elements: Polymer PTC resettable fuse (Replaces the blowable monitor-switch fuse and recovers after a fault.)
rationale: The user never faces a 'dead' oven that needs a service call.
judge_comment: Plausible component swap that avoids dead-oven failures, but it is only loosely tied to operational simplicity, and safety fuses in microwaves are regulated.

title: Optical Light-Curtain Interlock
new_elements: Infrared beam-break interlock (A single failsafe beam crossing the door gap cuts RF instantly.)
rationale: No precise door slam is needed for the oven to start.
judge_comment: An IR beam-break interlock could make door closing more forgiving, but safety certification generally requires redundant mechanical interlocks, and the benefit to ease of use is modest.

title: Glass Waveguide Window
new_elements: Flush borosilicate waveguide cover (Replaces flaky mica with a wipeable flush glass panel.)
rationale: There is no fragile part to clean carefully or replace.
judge_comment: A glass waveguide cover is plausible and easier to clean, but it only loosely serves the no-learning-curve operation need.

title: Certified Sealed RF Brick
new_elements: Potted pre-certified RF module (All HV and RF parts sealed in one certified brick.)
rationale: Enables ultra-simple casings and controls built around a safe core.
judge_comment: A sealed RF module is feasible and could simplify design, but the benefit to user simplicity is indirect.

title: Collapsible Mesh Cavity
new_elements: Foldable metal-mesh fabric cavity (A conductive textile pouch zips around the food on a base unit.)
rationale: Zip it and press go, folding away in a student dorm.
judge_comment: A conductive mesh pouch is a radical idea, but it has RF leakage, arcing and safety problems, and it does little for operational simplicity.

title: Thermochromic Done Lid
new_elements: Thermochromic splatter cover (Cover pigment turns from blue to red at about 70°C of food vapour.)
rationale: A colour change shows the food is hot, with no numbers to read.
judge_comment: A color-changing cover gives an easy visual doneness cue, but it doesn't substitute for operating the controls and it is an add-on.

title: Defrost Shield Sleeve
new_elements: Graded metal-mesh defrost sleeve (A perforated sleeve over the food passively reduces absorbed power; no power knob needed.)
rationale: Users choose 'gentle' by covering the food, a physical and intuitive act.
judge_comment: Creative passive power reduction, but metal mesh in a microwave risks arcing and the effect would be unpredictable, and users still need a time control.

title: Top-Loading Lid Oven
new_elements: Gravity-closed top lid (A lid on top seals by its own weight plus an interlock, with no latch mechanism.)
rationale: It works like a rice cooker or pot lid, an action everyone already knows.
judge_comment: Top-loading lid is a familiar action, but the benefit for operation simplicity is modest, and the cavity/choke seal and ergonomics are challenging.

title: Colour-Code Standard
new_elements: Colour-band knob matched to food stickers (The knob positions are coloured; food packs carry a matching colour dot.)
rationale: Users match colours instead of decoding instructions.
judge_comment: Colour matching is easy to follow but depends on food manufacturers adopting stickers, and it is not radical.

title: Vibrating Wristband Alert
new_elements: Paired haptic wrist tag (Buzzes when food is ready, replacing the bell for hard-of-hearing users.)
rationale: An end signal that cannot be missed means nothing to remember.
judge_comment: It's feasible and helpful for accessibility, but it only improves the end alert and does nothing for the operating learning curve.

title: Spring-Strap Self-Closing Hinge
new_elements: Single stamped spring-steel strap hinge (One part acts as both the hinge and a gentle self-closer.)
rationale: The door closes itself, so users never leave it ajar wondering why nothing works.
judge_comment: A self-closing spring hinge is plausible and cheap, but it only marginally addresses operation simplicity and is not radical.

title: Graduated Fill-Line Mug
new_elements: Time-marked heating mug (Fill lines read '1 min', '2 min', so the liquid level tells users which knob setting to pick.)
rationale: The container itself carries the instructions.
judge_comment: Instructions built into the mug are intuitive, but they work only for one container and one wattage, and the substitution is weak.

title: Weighing Turntable
new_elements: Load-cell floor (Replaces the glass turntable with a flat scale.); Weight-based timing (Calculates cook time from the food's mass.)
rationale: The user never has to estimate how many minutes a portion needs.
judge_comment: Weight-based timing helps, but mass alone doesn't determine the cook time, and it still needs a start control.

title: Transparent Conductive Door
new_elements: ITO-coated glass door (A clear RF-shielding film replaces the perforated mesh and the incandescent lamp.); Unobstructed viewing (Room light is enough to see the food clearly.)
rationale: The user can simply look at the food to judge progress.
judge_comment: A clear conductive door improves visibility, but it does little to simplify operation, and the RF shielding and cost are uncertain.

title: Heat-Colour Glow Ring
new_elements: RGB LED ring (Replaces the lamp and shifts from blue to red as the food warms.); Ambient heat feedback (Shows the food's temperature through colour.)
rationale: Blue means cold and red means hot, which anyone can read.
judge_comment: A colour ring is intuitive feedback, but it needs temperature sensing to work and only reports status, not operation.

title: Solid-State RF, No Turntable
new_elements: GaN solid-state RF (Phased RF sources steer heat evenly without moving parts.); Flat ceramic floor (Replaces the glass turntable.); Even heating without rotation (Food heats uniformly while sitting still.)
rationale: There is no turntable to seat, balance or wash.
judge_comment: It is a genuinely radical hardware swap, but solid-state RF at this power is costly, and the gain for operation simplicity is indirect.

title: Tap-the-Door Timer
new_elements: Door accelerometer (Each knock on the door adds 30 s.); Knock input (Uses the whole door as the input surface.)
rationale: Knocking is a natural action that needs no instruction.
judge_comment: Novel, but knocking is not an obvious affordance for a microwave and risks false triggers from door slams and vibrations.

title: Electronic Nose Stop
new_elements: MOX gas sensor (Smells scorching and stops the cycle.); Burn prevention (Catches the user's mistakes automatically.)
rationale: Getting the time wrong carries no penalty.
judge_comment: Gas-sensor burn detection is feasible and forgiving, though sensor-based cooking already exists and it only guards against errors rather than removing operation steps.

title: Habit-Learning Default
new_elements: Usage-pattern learning (Learns what the household usually heats at each time of day.); Predicted program (Pressing GO runs the most likely setting.)
rationale: The oven learns the user, so the user does not have to learn the oven.
judge_comment: Learning the household's habits means GO is the only input, but the mechanism is vague and wrong guesses could be unsafe or annoying.

title: Repeat-Last Button
new_elements: Again button (Reruns the previous cycle.); Zero-input repeat (Daily routines need no setting at all.)
rationale: It covers the most frequent use case with one press.
judge_comment: Simple and feasible, but many microwaves already have it and it is not radical.

title: Drawer Microwave
