new_elements: Wraparound mesh-glass cavity walls (Shielded glass on three sides lets room light illuminate the food, so no lamp is fitted.)
rationale: Food is visible from anywhere in the kitchen without the user doing anything.
judge_comment: Shielded glass walls on three sides are technically awkward, and ambient light is unreliable, so the link to simple operation is weak.

title: Glow-in-Dark Cavity
new_elements: Phosphorescent cavity enamel (The interior coating charges in room light and glows, replacing the incandescent lamp.)
rationale: Users can always see inside, with no bulb to replace.
judge_comment: A phosphorescent coating is cheap and simple, but it barely affects ease of operation and may degrade under heat and grease.

title: Skylight Cavity
new_elements: Shielded top skylight (A meshed glass roof panel lets room light fall into the cavity.)
rationale: With no bulb there is nothing to burn out or replace, and peeking from above is natural.
judge_comment: A skylight is a modest convenience; room light is often inadequate, and the roof opening is a leakage and cleaning concern.

title: Rice-Cooker Top Lid
new_elements: Top-loading flip lid (The cavity opens from the top like a rice cooker or kettle.)
rationale: It borrows the familiar rice-cooker way of loading food.
judge_comment: Top-loading is familiar from rice cookers, but it adds little to ease of operation and brings spill and leakage-seal problems.

title: Steam Whistle Alert
new_elements: Vent steam whistle (A kettle-style whistle in the exhaust sounds when the food releases steam.)
rationale: It uses the familiar kettle signal and needs no electronics.
judge_comment: A kettle-style whistle is a familiar cue, but steam release in a microwave is unreliable and a whistle doesn't simplify operation itself.

title: Reset-Button Breaker
new_elements: Resettable thermal breaker (A push-to-reset breaker on the back replaces the internal ceramic fuse.)
rationale: A trip is fixed by pressing a button rather than calling a technician.
judge_comment: Reasonable repair/safety swap, but barely touches the no-learning-curve operation need and is not radical.

title: Glowing Walls
new_elements: Electroluminescent cavity coating (Thin phosphor panels behind a glass liner light the whole cavity evenly.)
rationale: Shadow-free, permanent light needs no maintenance knowledge.
judge_comment: Even lighting has almost no bearing on ease of operation, and electroluminescent panels in a microwave cavity face durability and RF issues.

title: Fiber Light Pipe
new_elements: External LED with acrylic light pipe (The light source sits on the outside fascia and is piped into the cavity.)
rationale: The light can be swapped from outside like a remote battery, so no service knowledge is needed.
judge_comment: Easier bulb replacement does little for learning-free operation, though a light pipe is a plausible substitute.

title: Passive Chimney Cooling
new_elements: Heat-pipe chimney cooler (Heat pipes and a chimney replace the fan, so the oven is silent and its status is shown by light.)
rationale: With no fan, users never confuse fan noise after cooking with the oven still heating.
judge_comment: Removing the fan to avoid confusion is a tenuous link to ease of use, and passive cooling of a magnetron is questionable.

title: Snap-Fit Polymer Hinges
new_elements: Glass-filled polymer snap hinge molding (Molded hinge pins replace stamped and welded steel hinges.)
rationale: The cost saving is reinvested in simpler controls, at no extra cost to the user.
judge_comment: Cheaper hinges are a plausible substitution, but they barely touch the no-learning-curve need and are not radical.

title: Periscope-Free Glass Cube
new_elements: Fully glazed cavity with coated walls (All cavity walls are transparent-conductive-coated glass with no interior lamp.)
rationale: Users see their food from any angle and stop the oven when it looks right.
judge_comment: A fully glazed cavity improves visibility, but transparent coatings with no lamp are hard to make shielded and uniformly lit, and the link to operation is weak.

title: LED Filament Lamp
new_elements: Long-life LED cavity light (A 1 W LED behind a mesh lens that lasts the life of the product.)
rationale: Users never face a dark cavity or have to learn how to change a bulb.
judge_comment: A routine component swap with marginal link to learning-free operation.

title: Pop-Up Doneness Button
new_elements: Bimetal pop-up indicator probe (Like a turkey timer: pushed into the food, it pops up when the core is hot.)
rationale: A familiar, universal 'it popped, it's done' cue needs no explanation.
judge_comment: The familiar pop-up cue is simple, but a metal bimetal probe is unsafe in a microwave and the idea is not very novel.

title: Sealed Waveguide Window
new_elements: Flush glass-ceramic waveguide port (Replaces the fragile mica with a wipe-clean sealed port.)
rationale: There are no hidden parts that need special care or replacement.
judge_comment: A sealed port helps cleaning and maintenance but does little for operating simplicity or learning curve.

title: Cylindrical Cavity
new_elements: Cylindrical resonant cavity (The geometry gives naturally uniform field modes.)
rationale: Food can go anywhere and heat evenly.
judge_comment: Even heating helps a bit with ease of use, but it's a cavity geometry swap with only a weak link to learning curve, and it's not a cheaper/simpler substitute.

title: SiC Diode Stack
new_elements: Silicon-carbide HV diode (A more rugged replacement for the HV rectifier, reducing failures.)
rationale: Better reliability means users meet fewer confusing failures.
judge_comment: A SiC diode is an internal component swap that users never see, so it barely serves the simple-operation need.

title: Smart Plug Guardian
new_elements: Plug with thermal and current cutoff (The mains plug houses overheat and overload protection with a status LED.)
rationale: A single visible light shows whether everything is OK.
judge_comment: Safety plug barely affects operating simplicity and is not a radical substitution.

title: Self-Limiting PTC Protection
new_elements: PTC ceramic current limiter (Resistance rises sharply with heat, throttling power without nuisance trips.)
rationale: The oven self-recovers instead of mysteriously dying until a cooldown the user doesn't understand.
judge_comment: A protection component that is invisible to the user and barely affects operation, so it does little for the simplicity need.

title: Unbreakable Silicone Mat
new_elements: Food-grade silicone turntable mat (Flexible, dishwasher-safe, shatterproof.)
rationale: No careful handling required.
judge_comment: Silicone mat is shatterproof and easy to handle, but it is a modest swap with heat and flatness concerns and little impact on learning.

title: Unplug Auto-Shorting Relay
new_elements: Normally-closed discharge relay (Shorts the HV capacitor the instant mains is lost.)
rationale: The appliance is safe the moment it is unplugged, with no hidden hazard to know about.
judge_comment: An auto-discharge relay is a real safety feature, but it is invisible to the user and has little bearing on ease of operation.

title: Sealed Double-Insulated Core
new_elements: Potted sealed power module (All HV electronics encapsulated, Class II, no earth pin needed.)
rationale: Plugs into any socket safely, with no earthing caveats.
judge_comment: Potted Class II construction is feasible and removes earthing concerns, but it is a safety and installation matter, not an operation one.

title: Cordless Battery Microwave
new_elements: LiFePO4 battery pack (Stores enough energy for about ten 3-minute heats and recharges from any socket.)
rationale: The oven works anywhere, such as a desk, dorm or picnic, without any socket logistics.
judge_comment: A battery-powered microwave is radical but has little to do with simple operation, and the power draw (about 1 kW) makes it implausible.

title: Unbreakable Silicone Turntable Mat
new_elements: Microwave-safe silicone mat (A flexible, unbreakable mat replaces the heavy glass plate.)
rationale: There is nothing to break or position, and it can be rinsed and dropped back in.
judge_comment: Removes breakage and positioning concerns but barely affects operation, and silicone may not support a turntable well.

title: Long-Life LED Lamp
new_elements: 2 W sealed LED module (Cool, lifetime-rated light that never needs replacing.)
rationale: The user never has to learn how to replace a bulb hidden behind the cavity.
judge_comment: A sealed LED lamp is easy to build but is an obvious swap that barely addresses operating simplicity.

title: Cordless Countertop Pad
new_elements: Contact-pad power base (The microwave sits on a powered countertop pad with sprung contacts, so the unit itself has no cord.)
rationale: The user just sets it down and it works, with no plugging-in.
judge_comment: A cordless pad is novel, but the high power draw makes contacts hazardous, and the pad still has to be plugged in, so it mostly moves the cord.

title: Thermal Fuse in the Plug
new_elements: Plug-head thermal cutoff (Thermal protection and power-on indication moved into the plug.)
rationale: Users can see at the wall whether the unit is live and safe.
judge_comment: Moving the thermal fuse and live indication into the plug is somewhat odd, and a plug-head fuse would not sense cavity temperature, so it adds little to ease of use.

title: Capacitorless Ferroresonant Supply
new_elements: Ferroresonant HV transformer (Self-regulating transformer design that removes the need for a high-voltage capacitor.)
rationale: Eliminates a hazard that users would otherwise have to be warned about.
judge_comment: Ferroresonant supply is a real concept but it addresses a safety hazard, not operation simplicity, so it barely serves the need.

title: Waveguide Guillotine Shutter
new_elements: Door-linked metal waveguide shutter (Opening the door physically drops a plate across the waveguide, giving mechanical isolation alongside the electrical interlocks.)
rationale: Adds fail-safe, mechanical safety that is invisible to the user.
judge_comment: A mechanical safety shutter is invisible to the user and does nothing for operational simplicity, and microwaves already have door interlocks.

title: Lamp-Free Translucent Cavity
new_elements: Shielded translucent side panels (Ambient light enters through mesh-laminated panels, removing the 25 W lamp.)
rationale: Food is always visible from any angle, so there is nothing to check or switch.
judge_comment: Removing the lamp is a real substitution, but ambient light inside a closed cavity is often too dim and mesh panels add leakage risk, and the idea barely reduces operational complexity.

title: Conductive Gasket Seal
new_elements: Silver-filled silicone door gasket (An RF-tight elastomer replaces the precision quarter-wave choke.)
rationale: A forgiving seal stays safe even when the door is slammed or dirty.
judge_comment: A more forgiving seal improves robustness but barely changes operation, so it does little for the no-learning-curve need.

title: PTC Self-Limiting Magnetron Guard
new_elements: PTC ceramic thermistor in magnetron supply (Resistance spikes when hot, throttling power with no snapping parts.)
rationale: Silent self-protection means no unexplained shutdowns for users to puzzle over.
judge_comment: A PTC in a high-voltage magnetron supply is questionable, and the benefit to ease of use is only indirect.

title: Hinge-Driven Waveguide Shutter
new_elements: Mechanical waveguide shutter linked to hinge (Physically blocks RF when the door opens, replacing the monitor-switch fuse trick.)
rationale: Fail-safe by geometry, with no blown fuses that leave users confused.
judge_comment: A mechanical RF shutter is a safety substitution that users never see, so it does little for ease of operation and adds cost and complexity.

title: SiC Diode Stack
new_elements: Silicon-carbide HV rectifier (Lower loss and longer life than the silicon HV diode.)
rationale: Fewer failures mean the product just keeps working.
judge_comment: A SiC rectifier is a component swap with an invisible benefit to simplicity, and it is likely more expensive rather than simpler or cheaper.

title: Printed Mesh in Glass Door
new_elements: Transparent conductive-film door pane (An ITO or silver-nanowire film replaces the perforated metal screen.)
rationale: A clear view of the food removes the need to open and check.
judge_comment: A transparent conductive film could replace the metal mesh, but the benefit to operating simplicity is marginal, and the film's microwave shielding at 2.45 GHz is questionable.

title: Fused Interlock-in-Plug
new_elements: Smart plug with ground-fault and over-current trip (Moves protection out of the cavity into a resettable plug.)
rationale: A visible reset button replaces internal fuses users cannot service.
judge_comment: Moving protection into the plug is a plausible but safety-focused idea with little effect on operating simplicity, and removing internal safeguards is questionable.

title: Ever-Cool Exterior Casing
new_elements: Double-wall polymer shell (Replaces the painted steel wrap; stays touch-cool.)
rationale: No hot surfaces to learn to avoid.
judge_comment: A touch-cool casing is a real substitution, but it only loosely relates to ease of operation and is not radical.

title: Cheap LED Lamp
new_elements: LED interior light (A 1 W LED rated for a lifetime of use.)
rationale: The bulb never needs replacing, so there is no maintenance to learn.
judge_comment: An LED lamp is already standard and barely affects ease of operation.

title: Flat Wipe Floor
new_elements: Seamless glass-ceramic floor (A flush floor with no tray or rollers, used with the mode stirrer.)
rationale: Cleaning is a single wipe with no parts to remove.
judge_comment: This addresses cleaning rather than operation, so it barely serves the no-learning-curve need, though a glass floor is feasible.

title: Magnetic Breakaway Power Connector
new_elements: MagSafe-style mains connector (Snaps on and releases safely if the cord is yanked.)
rationale: The cord attaches by itself and cannot be plugged in wrongly.
judge_comment: A magnetic breakaway mains connector is a known concept and improves safety and setup, but it does not simplify cooking operation.

title: Glass-Ceramic Waveguide Window
new_elements: Flush glass-ceramic waveguide cover (Wipe-clean and does not burn like splattered mica.)
rationale: There is no fragile part that users need to know to keep clean.
judge_comment: It mainly addresses cleaning rather than operation, and the claimed no-learning benefit is weak.

title: Glowing Cavity Walls
new_elements: Electroluminescent cavity coating (Whole-wall soft light replaces the 25 W incandescent bulb.)
rationale: Food is shadow-free and visible, and there is no bulb to replace.
judge_comment: Electroluminescent walls are inside an RF cavity and would be hard to make robust, and the benefit to ease of use is marginal.

title: Conductive Polymer Housing
new_elements: Carbon-filled molded shielding shell (Replaces the stamped steel case with a single moulding.)
rationale: The rounded, light form can be shaped to make its use self-evident.
judge_comment: A conductive polymer shell is a real substitution, but achieving adequate microwave shielding is doubtful and the link to self-evident use is indirect.

title: Clear Conductive Glass Door
new_elements: ITO/silver-nanowire transparent conductive coating (Optically clear film that reflects 2.45 GHz radiation.); Mesh-free transparent door ()
rationale: Users see their food clearly without squinting through a dotted mesh.
judge_comment: A technically specific idea, but it barely affects ease of operation, and transparent coatings with adequate RF shielding and durability are hard to make.

title: Conductive Fabric Curtain
new_elements: Silver-textile magnetic-seam curtain door (Flexible conductive cloth with magnetic edges and seam-continuity interlock sensors.); Textile seam leakage verification ()
rationale: Users brush the curtain aside and drop the food in, with no hinges or latches.
judge_comment: Radical, but a flexible fabric door is very unlikely to contain microwave leakage safely, and seam sensing adds complexity.

title: Daylight Transparent Box
new_elements: ITO-coated glass cabinet and door (Transparent conductive coating gives RF shielding; ambient room light illuminates the food.)
rationale: The user can see everything at a glance, with no lamp to burn out.
judge_comment: Visibility helps a little, but it barely affects operation, and a transparent conductor on full glass faces absorption and shielding challenges.

title: Glowing Enamel Cavity
new_elements: Photoluminescent cavity enamel (Charged by an external LED through the door, the walls glow softly inside.)
rationale: The cavity is always visible and there is no bulb to replace.
judge_comment: Replaces the bulb with glowing enamel, but it does little for operational simplicity; the glow would also be dim and fade quickly.

title: Reset-Button Breaker
new_elements: Resettable thermal-magnetic breaker (Pop-out reset button replaces the sealed ceramic fuse)
rationale: A dead oven becomes a 'press reset' moment instead of a repair-technician visit.
judge_comment: A resettable breaker helps with recovery from faults, not with learning-free operation, so it is largely off-target.

title: Thermochromic Door Window
new_elements: Heat-reactive door glass band (A band on the window shifts colour with the cavity's air temperature, acting as a 'cooking in progress' indicator)
rationale: Users get passive, self-explaining state feedback with no electronics to understand.
judge_comment: A thermochromic band is a cheap, passive status indicator, but it only shows that cooking is happening (which the light and turntable already show) and does nothing to simplify the controls, so it's only marginally relevant; it's also not radical, and microwaves heat food rather than air, so the cavity air temperature is a weak and lagging signal.

title: Daylight Light Pipe
new_elements: 20-25 W incandescent lamp (Base interior lamp being substituted.); Waveguide-safe light pipe (A sub-cutoff acrylic rod channels room light into the cavity.)
rationale: Removes a bulb that fails and must be replaced, so there is no maintenance to learn.
judge_comment: A light pipe removes bulb maintenance but barely relates to operating without learning, and a dim cavity would hurt visibility.

title: Cordless Charging Pad
new_elements: Mains cord + plug (Base power connection being substituted.); Inductive countertop power pad (The oven sits on the pad and draws power with no cord.)
rationale: Set it down and it is ready to use.
judge_comment: A cordless pad removes a plug but does little for operation simplicity, and inductive power at ~1 kW is inefficient and impractical.

title: Glowing Cavity Walls
new_elements: Single incandescent lamp (Base interior lamp being substituted.); Electroluminescent cavity lining (Shadowless, even glow across the whole interior.)
rationale: Food is clearly visible from any angle.
judge_comment: Better interior lighting barely affects ease of operation, and electroluminescent lining in a microwave cavity is questionable.

title: Silicone Grip Mat
new_elements: Flexible silicone turntable mat (An unbreakable, dishwasher-safe mat keyed to the coupler that can be dropped in any way up.)
rationale: There is no fragile glass to align or fear breaking.
judge_comment: A silicone mat is simple and robust, but it only slightly reduces the learning curve and may not be microwave-safe or stable for rotation.

title: Self-Draining Transformer Winding
new_elements: Relay-shorted auxiliary winding (On power-off, a normally-closed relay dumps the capacitor charge through a winding.)
rationale: The appliance is inherently safe, so the user never has to know about hidden hazards.
judge_comment: Capacitor discharge is a safety feature the user never sees, so it does nothing for ease of operation, and it is an incremental fix.

title: Doubler-Free Half-Wave Drive
new_elements: Direct half-wave magnetron supply (A higher-ratio transformer feeds the magnetron directly without a storage capacitor.)
rationale: It is cheaper and carries no stored lethal charge.
judge_comment: It lowers cost and removes the stored charge, but users never see it and it does nothing for ease of operation; half-wave drive also stresses the tube.

title: Self-Rectifying Magnetron
new_elements: Magnetron self-rectification (The tube conducts only on one half-cycle, removing the HV diode.)
rationale: Fewer parts mean fewer failures for the user to cope with.
judge_comment: Removing the HV diode is a cost-saving internal change with no visible effect on how simple the product is to use.

title: Thermochromic Window
new_elements: Heat-sensitive door window tint (The inner glass turns red as rising cavity steam heats it.)
rationale: A red window intuitively means the food is hot.
judge_comment: Window tint changing with steam heat is a vague indicator, and the glass has a metal mesh and is not heated directly, so it only loosely helps operation and isn't a real substitution.

title: Nonstick Ceramic Cavity
new_elements: Sol-gel ceramic nonstick coating (Splatter wipes off with water alone.)
rationale: Cleaning needs no special products or technique.
judge_comment: A nonstick cavity eases cleaning but has nothing to do with operating the microwave.

title: Capacitor-Free Supply
new_elements: Direct-drive magnetron inverter (Avoids bulk HV storage, so nothing needs discharging.)
rationale: It removes a danger that users and repairers would otherwise need to be warned about.
judge_comment: It mainly benefits repairers, not users, and a magnetron without any HV storage is questionable technically.

title: Hardwired Wall Module
new_elements: Wall-box integrated microwave (Mounts into the wall like a light switch module, with no cord.)
rationale: It is always there and always ready, behaving like a household fixture rather than an appliance.
judge_comment: A wall-hardwired microwave does little for operation simplicity and adds installation and heat/ventilation issues, though the fixture framing is intriguing.

title: Snap-Fit Tool-Free Assembly
new_elements: Stamped snap-tab cavity assembly (Interlocking stamped tabs replace screws and welds.)
rationale: Lower cost funds the auto-sensing features that make operation effortless.
judge_comment: Snap-fit assembly is a manufacturing cost change that has only an indirect link to ease of use, and RF sealing makes it questionable.

title: Single-Shell Stamped Body
new_elements: Deep-drawn one-piece cavity shell (Cavity and casing formed in one draw with snap-fit panels.)
rationale: Seamless interior is cheaper to make and easier to wipe clean.
judge_comment: It is a manufacturing and cleaning change with almost no effect on learning curve, and a deep-drawn one-piece shell is hard to make and to fit with the RF parts.

title: Silicone Mat Turntable
new_elements: Unbreakable silicone tray mat (Replaces the glass plate and is dishwasher-safe.)
rationale: Nothing breaks and nothing needs careful handling.
judge_comment: A silicone mat is a plausible substitute for the glass plate and is easier to handle, but it only marginally helps operation, and its microwave behavior and ability to support loads and rotate are questionable.

title: Gentle Mug Sleeve
new_elements: Mesh-lined silicone sleeve for delicate items (A sleeve slows heating of milk or chocolate so it does not boil over.)
rationale: Power control becomes an accessory you slip on, so there are no levels to understand.
judge_comment: A mesh sleeve adds an accessory the user must learn, and the mesh risks sparks and heats inconsistently.

title: Light-Pipe Window
new_elements: Room-light pipe in cavity roof (Shielded acrylic light guide brings kitchen light into the cavity.)
rationale: Removing a part that can fail means one less thing for the user to deal with.
judge_comment: Replacing the cavity bulb with a light pipe barely touches operation simplicity, and a dim pipe may not light the interior well.

title: Silent Heat-Pipe Cooling
new_elements: Heat pipe to rear fin sink (Passive cooling of the RF source.)
rationale: Without fan noise, any sound the oven makes is clearly meaningful feedback.
judge_comment: Passive cooling is a quieter design but barely relates to operation simplicity, and the feedback rationale is weak.

title: No Stored Charge by Design
new_elements: Capacitor-free resonant HV converter (Stores negligible energy, so no bleeder discharge is needed.)
rationale: Users and repairers do not need to know about hidden lethal hazards.
judge_comment: It addresses hidden hazards for repairers, not user operation, and the capacitor-free HV claim is questionable.

title: Inherently Low-Risk Architecture
new_elements: 48 V SELV internal bus (All user-reachable electronics run at safe extra-low voltage.)
rationale: Safety is built in, so users get no warning labels to decode.
judge_comment: A 48 V SELV bus does little for operational simplicity, and the magnetron still needs high voltage, so it only loosely serves the need.

title: Glowing Cavity Walls
new_elements: Electroluminescent wall coating (Shadowless panel lighting built into the cavity enamel.); Even interior illumination (Replaces the 20-25 W incandescent bulb, which can burn out.)
rationale: Food is clearly visible, and there is no bulb to replace.
judge_comment: Replaces the bulb with electroluminescent walls, but this barely affects operational simplicity, and EL coating inside a microwave cavity is impractical (heat, RF, grease).

title: Forever Light
new_elements: Externally mounted LED with light pipe (A 1 W LED outside the cavity shines in through a sub-wavelength aperture.)
rationale: The light never burns out, so users never face a dark oven or a maintenance task.
judge_comment: Addresses bulb maintenance rather than operation simplicity, and a sub-wavelength aperture offers little light transmission.

title: Daylight Light Pipe
new_elements: Shielded light pipe channelling room light into the cavity (Replaces the 20-25 W lamp.)
rationale: The interior is visible without a bulb that can burn out.
judge_comment: Interesting bulb substitute, but it barely relates to operation simplicity and a dim cavity is a practical problem.

title: Self-Lighting Glow Cavity
new_elements: Phosphorescent cavity coating charged by the window and room light (The interior glows with no lamp.)
rationale: There is no bulb to replace, ever.
judge_comment: A phosphorescent coating would not survive microwave cavity conditions or give useful light, and it does little for ease of operation.

title: External LED Light Pipe
new_elements: Outside-mounted LED with acrylic light pipe (Light is piped in through a sub-wavelength aperture, so it never needs replacing.)
rationale: It removes a maintenance task the user would otherwise have to learn.
judge_comment: An external light pipe removes bulb maintenance but barely touches operating simplicity, and getting enough light through a sub-wavelength aperture is doubtful.
